title: Playbook Creator Playbook
description: Meta-playbook for creating domain-specific playbooks. Produces structured JSON playbooks through 16 phases of research, KB construction and bootstrapping, architecture, task engineering, assembly, validation, and structured dry-run. Works with single-agent systems where one agent fills multiple functional roles; output playbooks may optionally use role-based-multi-agent with per-role agent_assignment.
phase_summary: Phase 0: Commission & Scoping — Establish configuration (output location, external data permissions), define purpose, scope, constraints, complexity profile. Agent must acknowledge all 16 phases.
Phase 1: Domain Research — Research domain, best practices, SME knowledge, competitive landscape.
Phase 2: KB Architecture — CONDITIONAL (kb_mode=PLAYBOOK_MANAGED only) — Design knowledge base layers, schemas, bridge mappings, population strategy.
Phase 3: KB Bootstrapping — CONDITIONAL (kb_mode=PLAYBOOK_MANAGED only) — Create directory tree, seed entries, harvest research content, validate schema conformance.
Phase 4: Process Architecture — Design output playbook phase structure, task granularity, dependencies, gates.
Phase 5: Role Engineering — Define functional roles for the output playbook: who does what, who approves, decision authority.
Phase 6: Task Engineering — Write detailed task descriptions, execution guides, and templates for each phase.
Phase 7: Output Configuration — Define workflow model, roles, usage instructions, compilation tuning, KB mapping.
Phase 8: Metrics & KPI Definition — Define process, quality, and domain outcome metrics with targets.
Phase 9: JSON Assembly — Assemble complete output playbook JSON from all design documents.
Phase 10: JSON Validation & Consistency — Validate assembled JSON using automated validators and manual review.
Phase 11: Quality Audit — Gap Analysis — Systematic audit against requirements, cross-cutting concerns, and completeness.
Phase 12: Stress Testing & Structured Dry-Run — Walk through the playbook under structured scenarios to find issues.
Phase 13: Stakeholder Review & Iteration — Final human review before pilot testing.
Phase 14: Documentation & Version Control — Package the final playbook with supporting documentation.
Phase 15: Continuous Improvement — After each run of the output playbook, review and optionally improve it.

capability_assessment._description: Maps each phase to a minimum CAPABILITY TIER (frontier/high/fast), provider-agnostic. Resolve a tier to a concrete model via defaults.providers[defaults.provider]. If the executing model is below a phase's minimum tier, trigger the accommodations. Legacy model-name tiers (opus/sonnet/haiku) still resolve via defaults.tier_aliases.

tiers.frontier: Full capability — executes all phases as written. E.g. Claude Opus 5 (Max), GPT-5.5.
tiers.high: Strong — split Phase 9 (JSON Assembly) into 2 sessions and add extra validation in Phases 10-12. E.g. Claude Sonnet 5.
tiers.fast: Basic — one phase per session; automated gate validation only (no self-assessment); skip subjective audit dimensions (detail calibration, completability) in Phase 11. E.g. Claude Haiku 4.5.

accommodations.below_minimum: If executing model is below phase_minimums for a phase: (1) split the phase into 2 sessions, (2) use automated gate verification exclusively (no self-assessment), (3) reduce compilation block context to essential files only, (4) record the accommodation in decisions-ledger.md

capability_assessment.claude_code_max_profile: DEFAULT target: on the Claude Code Max plan with high budget, run ALL phases at 'frontier' (Claude Opus 5). phase_minimums are FLOORS for constrained or non-Claude providers, not targets — with Max, correctness/consistency is the binding constraint, not cost, so do not down-tier reasoning-heavy phases (9, 11) to save budget.

provider_profiles.anthropic_max: Frontier everywhere (Opus 5). No accommodations needed; 200K window (1M available) means most phases fit one session — still break Phase 13 for genuine human input.
provider_profiles.openai_codex: gpt-5.5 is a single frontier-class model, so it meets every phase_minimum; but because there is no cheaper tier to fall back to, keep the session-splitting discipline on the heavy phases (9, 11-12) and rely on automated gate verification. Run inside the Codex sandbox per ~/AGENTS.md.
provider_profiles.other: Map your models to tiers in defaults.providers.generic; if your strongest model is below 'frontier' class, apply accommodations on phases 9 and 11 and prefer automated validation.

anthropic._note: Claude Code Max plan, high budget — DEFAULT. Prefer frontier; budget is not the binding constraint.

openai_codex._note: OpenAI Codex CLI (gpt-5.5). Single strong model across tiers; still apply the 'fast/high' session-splitting + extra-validation accommodations because it is one model, and honor the Codex sandbox (per ~/CODEBUDDY.md / ~/AGENTS.md).

generic._note: Any other agent system: map your strongest/mid/fast models to these tiers.

Coordinator.description: Phase gates, tracking, status updates, blocker escalation, decisions ledger and artifact manifest maintenance
Coordinator.role_context: Track progress systematically. Verify conditions before advancing. Maintain decisions-ledger and artifact-manifest at every gate.

Researcher.description: Domain research, best practices, SME knowledge, competitive analysis
Researcher.role_context: Gather broadly, synthesize precisely. Cite sources. Distinguish facts from opinions. Flag gaps in knowledge.

Architect.description: Phase structure, task granularity, role design, dependency mapping, template design
Architect.role_context: Design for clarity and separation. Every boundary must be justified. Every dependency must be explicit. Favor simplicity.

Builder.description: Task titles/descriptions, JSON assembly, validation, implementation of fixes
Builder.role_context: Mechanical precision. Follow specifications exactly. Verify output matches input requirements. No creative interpretation during assembly.

Auditor.description: Quality review, scenario walkthroughs, gap analysis, stress testing, failure mode cataloging, contamination testing, final verification before handoff
Auditor.role_context: Binary yes/no judgments, no hedging. Find what is broken. Review with fresh eyes. Do not defend previous work.

Stakeholder.description: Purpose, scope, constraints, success criteria, business decisions, final approval
Stakeholder.role_context: Business alignment. Does this serve the commission? Are constraints respected? Would you trust this playbook to run unsupervised?

in_scope: Knowledge base bootstrapping (directory creation, placeholder seeding, initial harvesting)
Structured dry-run validation with scenario matrix
out_of_scope: Executing the produced playbook (that is the user's responsibility)
Full KB curation and ongoing maintenance (the creator bootstraps the KB with placeholders and initial harvesting; full curation is the user's responsibility)
Multi-agent orchestration of the creation process itself (the creator runs as single-agent; output playbooks may use role-based-multi-agent with per-role agent_assignment)
adjacent: Skills/prompting frameworks that may be activated per-phase
Knowledge bases built from the produced KB specification
CI/CD or version control for produced playbooks

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Quality Standard
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Every produced playbook must be comprehensive enough that any team can execute it without ambiguity. Every task must have an owner. Every non-obvious task must have a description. Every phase must have a gate with explicit conditions. No placeholder content.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Embed as a verification checklist item in task descriptions where this concern applies. The item must be a concrete yes/no check, not a restatement of the concern.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Role Consistency
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Roles defined at playbook start must be used consistently throughout all tasks. Every task title must start with [Role]. Roles cannot appear fewer than 3 times (orphaned) or reference undefined roles.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Include role consistency verification as an explicit gate condition at phases where tasks are written or assembled.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Gate Enforcement
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Phase gates are firewall points — nothing advances until all conditions are met. Each gate must list explicit conditions, blocker examples, and handoff blocks. Conditions must be verifiable, not subjective.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Include gate completeness as a pre_check condition in compilation blocks for phases that define or validate gates.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Deliverable Tracking
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Every task that produces output must name the file path. The artifact manifest and metrics tracker are persistent files that must be updated at every phase gate. Later phases reference earlier deliverables through handoff chains.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Every task that produces a deliverable must have an 'output' field with the exact file path. At every phase gate: (1) artifact-manifest.md must be updated to reflect all files produced in that phase, (2) metrics-tracker.md must be updated with any measurable metrics from that phase. Stale persistent files (not updated since a prior phase) are a gate failure.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Context Preservation
cross_cutting_concerns.description: decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, and metrics-tracker.md are persistent tracking files. decisions-ledger and artifact-manifest are loaded in every phase and updated at every gate. No decision rationale is silently lost across session boundaries.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Verify decisions-ledger.md and artifact-manifest.md appear in every phase's context_load (except Phase 0). Verify both are updated at every gate.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Gate Verification
cross_cutting_concerns.description: At every phase gate, the executing agent must produce a GATE VERIFICATION block listing each condition with explicit PASS or FAIL and a one-line evidence citation (file path or content reference). No condition may be marked PASS without evidence. A single FAIL blocks advancement.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Every gate task description must require the agent to output the verification block format. Gates without explicit PASS/FAIL evidence are treated as not checked.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Path Configuration Compliance
cross_cutting_concerns.description: All file operations use configured paths from Phase 0. No hardcoded external paths. File paths referenced in handoffs and context_load must match actual produced file paths.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Every phase that reads external files must reference paths from scope.md configuration section. At gates, verify output file paths match what was specified in task output fields.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Automated Gate Verification
cross_cutting_concerns.description: At least 50% of gate conditions at every phase must be verified by automated checks (file existence, JSON validation, word count thresholds, schema conformance) rather than agent self-assessment alone. The agent writes; tooling verifies.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Every gate task must include a 'gate_verification' sub-block listing automated checks to run. At least half of gate_conditions must have a corresponding automated check. Gates without automated verification evidence are treated as self-assessed and flagged.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Quality Regression Check
cross_cutting_concerns.description: At checkpoint phases, re-verify a sample of earlier deliverables still meet their original gate conditions. Quality established in early phases must not degrade silently in later phases.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: At Phases 6, 9, 12, and 14: pick 2-3 deliverables from earlier phases and verify they still meet their original quality bar. Report any regressions. If regression found, fix before advancing.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Team Completeness & Ownership
cross_cutting_concerns.description: In the produced playbook, every task owner must resolve to a defined role, every role must own at least one task (no defined-but-unused roles), and no task may be ownerless. The execution team must exactly cover the work — no orphan tasks, no idle agents.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Phase 5 gate and Phase 9/10 validation cross-check task owners against the role roster. validate_semantic fails on any owner not in roles{} and warns on any role that owns no task.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Independent Verification
cross_cutting_concerns.description: No artifact in the produced playbook may be verified by the same role that produced it. The team must contain at least one independent Verifier (Auditor/Reviewer/QA) whose gates check other roles' outputs.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Phase 5 gate asserts producer != verifier per artifact class and that an independent Verifier exists; Phase 11/12 audits are owned by that Verifier, never by the producing role.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Evidence Traceability (harvested playbooks)
cross_cutting_concerns.description: When commission_source=session_history, every failure mode, domain pattern, and decision carried into the produced playbook must cite the session/segment it was extracted from. Single-occurrence observations are flagged, not promoted to rules, until a second run confirms them.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Phase 1 ingest verifies citations and drops/flags uncited items; Phase 11 audit and Phase 12 dry-run re-check that harvested rules are supported before they gate anything.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Establish configuration
items.description:
Ask the user to establish runtime configuration before any other work begins:

1. OUTPUT LOCATION
   - Default: ~/playbooks/<playbook-name>/
   - Ask: "Save location: ~/playbooks/<playbook-name>/ — correct, or specify different path?"
   - If user specifies different path: use exact path provided
   - If directory exists: create ~/playbooks/<playbook-name>-v2/ (or next available: -v3, -v4, etc.)
   - Never merge or replace existing content in any directory

2. EXTERNAL DATA SOURCES
   - First, list available sources with numbered labels:
     * [1] Knowledge base at [path]
     * [2] Other playbooks at [path]
     * [3] References at [path]
   - Then ask: "Include any external sources? Options: 'none', 'all', or specify which (e.g., '1 and 3', 'all except 2')"
   - User can respond with:
     * "none" or "no" — skip all sources, document "No external data sources required"
     * "all" — include all listed sources
     * Numbers/names — include only specified sources (e.g., "1 and 3", "just the knowledge base")
     * "all except N" — include all except specified
   - Record all decisions in scope.md configuration section
   - Only access sources user explicitly approved
   - If no sources available or no external sources needed, document "No external data sources required"

Output: scope.md with configuration section documenting all decisions.

3. COMMISSION SOURCE
   - Ask: "What is this playbook built from? 'fresh' (new commission), 'session_history' (distil a prior AI-assisted build), or 'existing_playbook_revision' (revise a playbook you already have)?"
   - fresh (default): proceed normally.
   - session_history: a session harvest is REQUIRED as input. If one does not yet exist, run the front-end prompt `prompts/playbook-updater.md` against the raw transcript FIRST to produce `research/session-harvest.md`; Phase 1 then ingests and validates it.
   - existing_playbook_revision: the prior playbook is input for the Phase 1 audit task.
   - Record commission_source in decisions-ledger.md; it drives the router.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Decide knowledge base strategy
items.description:
Choose the KB strategy for the playbook being created. This decision controls whether Phases 2 and 3 run.

Ask the user:
"Does the output playbook need a knowledge base? If so, who manages it?"

Options:
1. PLAYBOOK_MANAGED — the output playbook will instruct agents to build and maintain their own KB during execution. Phases 2 and 3 will run to design and bootstrap it.
2. EXTERNAL_DIFY_MCP — KB is hosted externally (e.g., Dify) and exposed via MCP or API. The playbook will reference it by tool name. Phases 2 and 3 are skipped.
3. USER_SUPPLIED — the user will populate a KB/ folder in the output directory manually with their own files. A KB/ folder will be created in Phase 0. Phases 2 and 3 are skipped.
4. NONE — the output playbook does not need a KB. Phases 2 and 3 are skipped.

Record the decision:
- In scope.md under '## KB Strategy': record kb_mode value and one-line rationale
- In decisions-ledger.md: record the decision with timestamp

Default: if the user cannot decide, prompt: 'If you plan to use Dify or will supply files yourself, choose EXTERNAL_DIFY_MCP or USER_SUPPLIED. If unsure, choose NONE — you can add a KB later.'

If EXTERNAL_DIFY_MCP: also ask for the MCP tool name or API endpoint so it can be referenced in the output playbook.

FIDELITY TRADEOFF (audit 2026-09-18 F7): NONE = a PORTABLE playbook that regenerates implementation from task text (best for capturing a CLASS of work); USER_SUPPLIED = higher-fidelity for rebuilding an EXACT target (seed the KB/ folder with the reference implementation + findings). Choose by whether the goal is a class or an exact clone. State the choice + its fidelity consequence in scope.md.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Create project knowledge base folder
items.description:
Folder structure: README.md, research/, architecture/, drafts/, audits/, testing/, final/

Initialize decisions-ledger.md — empty, with header: '# Decisions Ledger — append at every phase gate'

Initialize artifact-manifest.md — empty, with header: '# Artifact Manifest — update at every phase gate' and columns: File | Phase | Status | Summary

Initialize metrics-tracker.md — empty, with header: '# Metrics Tracker — record at every phase gate' and columns: Metric | Phase | Value | Target | Date

KB FOLDER (conditional):
- If kb_mode == USER_SUPPLIED: create KB/ subdirectory in the output playbook directory. Create KB/README.md with content: "Place your knowledge base files here. The output playbook will reference this folder for KB access. Organize by topic subdirectory if needed."
- If kb_mode == EXTERNAL_DIFY_MCP or NONE: no KB/ folder needed. Record "KB folder not created — kb_mode={value}" in artifact-manifest.md.
items.output: README.md, project folder structure, decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, metrics-tracker.md

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Define the playbook's purpose and problem statement
items.description:
Answer precisely:
- What process does this playbook automate/guide?
- What problem does it solve? What goes wrong without it?
- Is this new, an optimization of existing, or a variant?

One paragraph, no ambiguity.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Define target users and team composition
items.description:
Who will RUN this playbook?
- Team size, roles, skill levels
- What tools/access do they have?

The playbook's detail level is calibrated to the least experienced person who will use it.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Define scope boundaries
items.description:
IN SCOPE: what this playbook covers
OUT OF SCOPE: what it does NOT cover
ADJACENT: what it connects to but doesn't own

Scope creep is the #1 killer of playbook quality.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Define success criteria for the playbook itself
items.description:
Measurable criteria (e.g., 'an unfamiliar user can execute it without clarifying questions')
Quality bar (e.g., 'every task has an owner, description, and exit criteria')
Pilot test pass/fail criteria

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Define strategic constraints
items.description:
Technology constraints, methodology constraints, budget/resource constraints, timeline constraints, compliance/legal constraints.

These become universal rules that every phase must respect.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Identify related existing playbooks
items.description:
Playbooks covering overlapping territory, upstream/downstream dependencies, reference/inspiration sources.

If replacing an existing playbook, that playbook becomes input for Phase 1 audit.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Classify domain complexity
items.description:
Answer three questions to set complexity guardrails for the creation process:

1. PROCESS COMPLEXITY: How many distinct phases does the real-world process have?
   - Simple (1-4 phases): single-skill workflow, linear steps
   - Standard (5-10 phases): multi-skill workflow, some parallelism
   - Complex (11+ phases): multi-discipline workflow, significant dependencies

2. KNOWLEDGE COMPLEXITY: How many distinct types of knowledge does the domain require?
   - Flat (1 type): single reference layer, no translation needed
   - Layered (2-3 types): multiple knowledge domains, some cross-referencing
   - Bridged (4+ types): distinct vocabularies that need translation between them

3. ROLE COMPLEXITY: How many distinct functional roles does the process need?
   - Minimal (2 roles): one doer, one approver
   - Standard (3-4 roles): specialized functions with handoffs
   - Full (5+ roles): distinct disciplines with complex handoff chains

Record the complexity_profile in decisions-ledger.md:
  process: simple|standard|complex
  knowledge: flat|layered|bridged
  roles: minimal|standard|full
  overall: highest of the three dimensions

The overall classification sets advisory guardrails (not hard limits) for the rest of the creation process.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Read and acknowledge all phases
items.description:
Read this playbook's phase_summary field (or scan all phase titles and purposes). Produce a one-line summary per phase in decisions-ledger.md under heading '## Phase Inventory'. This ensures the executing agent knows the full 16-phase scope before starting work.

Do NOT skip this task. Execution collapse (FM-026) occurs when an agent reads only early phases and synthesizes later ones from imagination.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Estimate context budget and plan session boundaries
items.description:
CONTEXT BUDGET ESTIMATION:
Estimate the total context needed for this playbook run:
1. This PBCPB file: ~83K tokens
2. Commission brief: estimate from user's input length
3. Research documents (Phase 1): typically 10-30K tokens total
4. KB entries (Phase 3): estimate based on complexity_profile.knowledge (flat: ~5K, layered: ~20K, bridged: ~50K+)
5. Architecture docs (Phase 4-6): typically 10-20K tokens
6. Assembled JSON (Phase 9): typically 15-40K tokens

If total estimated context exceeds the executing model's context window (resolve from defaults.providers[provider].window_tokens — e.g. Claude 5 ~200K, up to 1M; GPT-5.5 per its spec), identify which phases MUST run in fresh sessions to avoid context overflow.

SESSION BOUNDARY PLANNING:
Based on the session_strategy in this playbook's usage_instructions AND the context budget estimate, document planned session breaks in decisions-ledger.md. Record which phases share sessions and where fresh sessions start.

CRITICAL: The design-to-assembly transition (Phase 8 → Phase 9) is the highest-risk overflow point. If budget is tight, this MUST be a fresh session break with explicit state serialization (all decisions, artifacts, and KB status written to persistent files before break).

Session breaks should align with phase gates where decisions-ledger.md is updated.

Verify: every phase (0-15) appears in exactly one session group. No phase is orphaned or double-counted.

blocker_examples: scope.md missing configuration section — ask user for output location and external data permissions before proceeding
Purpose statement says 'improve the process' without specifying which process or what improvement looks like — too vague, rewrite
Scope has no out-of-scope list — everything is implicitly in scope, which means scope creep is guaranteed

checklists.title: Phase 1: Domain Research & Process Discovery
checklists.purpose: Understand the domain deeply enough to build a playbook for it. Research produces flat documents that Phase 2 will structure.

compilation.role_mindset: Researcher — gather, synthesize, document. Breadth over depth at this stage.
compilation.objective: Produce comprehensive flat research documents covering domain processes, best practices, competitors, cross-cutting concerns, and platform specifics
success_criteria: Domain analysis covers standard processes, failure modes, and terminology
Best practices documented with sources
Cross-cutting concerns identified with justification
Requirements document synthesizes all research

items.title: [Researcher] — Research the domain this playbook serves
items.description:
Standard processes in this industry/discipline, common failure modes, regulatory/compliance requirements, standard tools and platforms, terminology glossary, KPIs professionals track.

Source requirements: research must include at least one external source beyond any existing playbook or user-provided material. Use web search, documentation sites, published standards, or authoritative references. Cite every factual claim with its source. If replacing an existing playbook, the existing playbook is input data, not a substitute for fresh domain research.

items.title: [Researcher] — Research industry best practices and standards
items.description: Published standards (ISO, industry frameworks), expert recommendations (books, courses, authoritative sources), common process frameworks, typical phase structures, common pitfalls and how experts avoid them.

items.title: [Researcher] — Competitive playbook/template audit
items.description: Existing playbooks, templates, SOPs, checklists covering similar territory. For each: what it covers, what it does well, what it misses, structure, detail level.
items.conditional: Only if comparable playbooks/templates exist for this domain

items.title: [Researcher] — Audit existing playbook(s) being replaced
items.conditional: Only if replacing an existing playbook
items.description: What the existing playbook does well (KEEP), what it does poorly (FIX), what it's missing (ADD), what contradicts current strategy (REMOVE).

items.title: [Researcher] — Ingest and validate the session harvest
items.description:
Consume `research/session-harvest.md` (produced by the front-end prompt `prompts/playbook-updater.md`). Treat it as EVIDENCE, not truth:
1. Verify every extracted item cites the session/segment it came from; drop or flag any that don't (CCC-12).
2. Mark single-occurrence patterns 'verify in future runs' rather than promoting them to rules.
3. Seed the working failure-mode set from the harvest AND from PBCPB's existing failure-mode catalog (reuse ids where a known FM matches; mint new FM-NNN only for genuinely new ones).
4. Fold the harvested domain patterns/algorithms into the domain research docs; if they are substantial, plan a KB layer for them (Phase 2, kb_mode=USER_SUPPLIED) instead of inlining.
5. Carry the harvested creative-decision points forward as candidate human/Operator gates for Phase 5 role derivation.
The harvest informs requirements; it does not bypass Phases 4-15.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Gather process knowledge from subject matter experts
items.description:
The actual process (not documented — the real one), steps that aren't written down, common blockers and resolutions, decisions requiring judgment vs always-the-same, what they wish they'd known before their first time.

Self-service fallback: if the commissioning user IS the domain expert (no external SMEs available), conduct a structured self-interview. Ask the user the same questions you would ask an SME: what steps are undocumented, what commonly goes wrong, what requires judgment. Record their answers in the same sme-interviews.md format. The key insight must still be captured even if the source is the user rather than a third-party expert.

items.title: [Researcher] — Identify cross-cutting concerns
items.description:
Concerns that touch every phase, not just one. Technology/platform concerns affecting all phases. Compliance concerns applying to every task. Quality standards verified at every phase. Strategic constraints shaping every decision.

Cross-cutting concerns must be woven throughout the playbook, not isolated in one phase.

items.title: [Researcher] — Identify platform/environment-specific concerns
items.description: If the playbook involves a specific platform or environment: how does data/content get stored, what are the safe modification methods, what should NEVER be done (anti-patterns), what platform-specific tools exist, what deployment/migration procedures apply.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Synthesize research into requirements document
items.description: Domain requirements (what the process must accomplish), quality requirements (standards and compliance), strategic requirements (business constraints from Phase 0), platform requirements (technical constraints), cross-cutting requirements, user requirements (what the target team needs to succeed).

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Domain researched, requirements synthesized
gate_conditions: Domain analysis covers standard processes, failure modes, and terminology
Best practices documented with cited external sources (not solely derived from existing playbooks or user-provided material)
Competitive templates audited with strengths/weaknesses
Cross-cutting concerns identified with justification
Requirements document synthesizes all research
blocker_examples: Domain analysis missing key compliance requirements — research more
No SME input gathered — interview at least one expert before proceeding
Requirements document has 'TBD' sections — complete before proceeding

checklists.title: Phase 2: KB Architecture
checklists.purpose:
CONDITIONAL PHASE — only runs when kb_mode == PLAYBOOK_MANAGED (set in Phase 0 scope.md). If kb_mode is EXTERNAL_DIFY_MCP, USER_SUPPLIED, or NONE: skip this entire phase and proceed to Phase 4.

Convert flat research into a structured, queryable knowledge specification. This phase produces a KB ARCHITECTURE (blueprint), not the KB itself. The actual KB gets built when the output playbook is executed.

compilation.role_mindset: Architect — structuring knowledge, not gathering it. Classify, separate, define schemas.
compilation.objective: Produce a KB architecture blueprint (layers, schemas, bridge, population strategy) that an agent can build from without ambiguity
pre_check: Check scope.md kb_mode. If kb_mode != PLAYBOOK_MANAGED: SKIP this phase — record 'Phase 2 skipped: kb_mode={value}' in artifact-manifest.md and proceed to Phase 3 skip check.

items.title: [Architect] — Determine KB complexity level
items.description:
Decision question: 'Do users of this playbook describe goals in language that differs from implementation language?'
  YES → structured KB with bridge layer needed (e.g., audio: 'warm' → filter cutoff 0.2-0.4)
  NO → assess if domain has enough distinct knowledge types to warrant layers

Decision question: 'Does this domain have enough distinct knowledge types to justify separate layers?'
  YES → multi-layer KB (define layers)
  NO → flat reference (single folder of markdown files with table of contents)

If structured KB selected, also specify web harvesting configuration: which backends are available (ddg+webfetch, websearch+webfetch, webfetch, firecrawl, imported), default quality threshold (0.0-1.0), and max URLs per session.

The minimal path is genuinely minimal: single reference layer, no bridge, no cross-references, flat file list. A folder of markdown with a TOC. That is the floor.

items.title: [Architect] — Define knowledge layers
items.conditional: Only if multi-layer KB was chosen in Task 1
items.description:
For each layer: name and domain boundary (what belongs here and what doesn't), authority score (0.0-1.0), separation rule (why this can't merge with another layer), topics within the layer.

For each layer, also specify which harvesting backends are appropriate for that layer's content: ddg+webfetch (DuckDuckGo + WebFetch), websearch+webfetch (WebSearch + WebFetch), webfetch (direct URL), firecrawl (requires API key), imported (from external KB). Not all layers need the same backends.

Separation principle: knowledge that changes independently lives in separate layers.

items.title: [Architect] — Define KB entry schema
items.description:
Exact JSON structure every entry must follow.

Required fields: id ({kb-name}_{topic}_{entry-name}), kb (which layer), topic, status (placeholder|harvested|curated|synced), version (semver), title, summary, description, source, concepts (array of {name, description, related[]}), code_blocks (array of {language, code, preserved} — if domain involves code), tags, related_topics, difficulty (beginner|intermediate|advanced), domain_relevance (1-10).

Additional domain-specific fields defined here.

items.title: [Architect] — Define bridge entry schema
items.conditional: Only if KB complexity decision identified a need for creative-to-technical translation
items.description:
Bridge entry required fields: category, parameters (array), intent_mappings keyed by subjective descriptor with: parameter, value_range [min, max], typical_default, confidence (0.0-1.0), source, why (human-readable rationale), anti_patterns.

Bridge is hybrid: pre-seeded with common mappings from research, auto-generated when agent encounters unmapped concepts, feedback-enriched when user evaluation refines entries.

Combination layer: bridge entries can be composed. Cross-reference individual entries, identify compatible parameter ranges, flag conflicts between anti_patterns, propose combined recipe with lower confidence score.

items.title: [Architect] — Define population strategy
items.description:
Placeholder seeding: what entries get created as placeholders during playbook setup (minimum one per topic per layer, with fallback content).
Harvesting: where content comes from, quality criteria for harvested content.
Curation rules: what must happen before harvested content becomes curated.
Sync rules: how curated entries get indexed.
Versioning protocol: entries are append-only. Existing entries are never edited — they are superseded by new entries tagged with the relevant version. Old entries remain for reference or rollback. Queries filter by version tag.

Web harvesting configuration (for structured KBs):
- backends: array of enabled backends (ddg+webfetch, websearch+webfetch, webfetch, firecrawl, imported)
- domain_rankings: object mapping domain strings to authority scores (e.g., {"docs.juce.com": 0.95, "forum.cabbage.com": 0.7})
- quality_threshold: minimum confidence score for harvested entries (default 0.7)
- max_urls_per_session: maximum URLs to process per harvest session (default 5)

items.title: [Architect] — Specify KB access patterns
items.conditional: Only if multi-layer KB was chosen in Task 1
items.description:
Define how agents will query the KB during playbook execution:

1. Query patterns: What questions will agents ask of this KB? List typical query types.
2. Cross-layer queries: Which queries span multiple layers? How should results be merged?
3. Bridge queries: If bridge layer exists, what creative-to-technical translations will be needed?
4. Harvesting triggers: When should agents harvest new content? (user request, gap detected, periodic refresh)

Output: kb-access-spec.md documenting query patterns, expected query types per layer, and harvesting triggers.

items.title: [Architect] — Define index and directory structure
items.description:
Master index format (registry of all KBs, cross-topic mappings), per-KB index format (file listing by topic), per-KB manifest format (file status and sync history), cross-reference rules (results ranked by authority score), file naming conventions, exact directory tree.

KB registry: specify the path to the KB registry file (typically ~/.claude/kb-registry.json). The registry tracks all KB layers, their locations, and metadata for cross-KB queries. Each layer entry in the registry includes: name, path, domain_boundary, authority_score, and topics.

items.title: [Builder] — Create KB directory tree
items.description:
Create the exact directory tree specified in directory-structure.md. Every directory in the tree must exist. Every _archive subdirectory must exist. Create master-index.json at the root. Create per-layer manifest.json files.

Verify: directory count matches directory-structure.md specification exactly.
items.output: kb/ directory tree, master-index.json, per-layer manifest.json files

items.title: [Builder] — Register KB layers
items.description: Populate kb-registry.json with layer metadata from kb-architecture.md. Each layer entry includes: name, path (relative to ~/.claude/), domain_boundary, authority_score, topics array. The registry enables cross-KB queries and provides metadata for authority-weighted result ranking. Create the registry file at ~/.claude/kb-registry.json if it doesn't exist, or append to existing registry if other KBs are already registered.

items.title: [Builder] — Seed placeholder entries
items.description:
Create one placeholder entry per topic per layer as defined in population-strategy.md. Each placeholder must conform to entry-schema.json with status="placeholder" and empty content fields.

Verify: placeholder count matches the topic count from kb-architecture.md.

EXECUTION: Work one KB layer at a time. Seed all placeholders for the first layer, then the second, and so on. Update the per-layer manifest.json after completing each layer. Do not attempt all layers in a single response.
items.output: kb/ placeholder entries (one per topic per layer)

items.title: [Coordinator] — Seeding milestone gate: all placeholders created
items.description:
MILESTONE GATE — verify seeding is complete before transitioning to harvesting. This is a different cognitive mode: seeding is mechanical (Builder), harvesting is analytical (Researcher). Do NOT skip this checkpoint.

Verify:
1. Placeholder count matches topic count from kb-architecture.md
2. Every placeholder conforms to entry-schema.json with status='placeholder'
3. Per-layer manifest.json files reflect actual placeholder counts
4. Directory tree matches directory-structure.md

If any check fails, fix before proceeding to harvesting.
milestone_gate_conditions: Placeholder count matches kb-architecture.md topic count
All placeholders have status='placeholder' and conform to entry-schema.json

items.title: [Researcher] — Harvest initial content from research documents
items.description:
ROLE CHANGE: This task requires Researcher mindset (analytical extraction), not Builder mindset (mechanical creation). Read research documents carefully and extract substantive content.

Walk through research/domain-analysis.md, research/best-practices.md, and research/cross-cutting-concerns.md. For each knowledge item that maps to a KB entry, update the placeholder with harvested content and change status from "placeholder" to "harvested".

Harvested entries must have:
- description field >100 characters of substantive content (not boilerplate)
- concepts array populated with at least 2 entries
- source.reference citing the specific research document and section
- tags array populated

If replacing an existing playbook and its KB data was flagged for harvest in Phase 1, include that source.

Update per-layer manifest.json and master-index.json with entry counts.

Quality gate: harvested entries must cite their source document and section.

EXECUTION: Harvest one KB layer at a time. Complete all harvesting for the first layer, update its manifest, then proceed to the next layer. Do not attempt all layers in a single response.

CRITICAL: Count placeholder entries remaining after harvesting. If any entry accessible from research still has status='placeholder', this task is NOT complete. The Phase 3 gate will verify zero skipped harvestable entries.

Output: kb/ harvested entries, updated manifests

items.title: [Researcher] — Generate web harvest search terms
items.conditional: Only if structured KB and web harvesting enabled
items.description:
For each KB layer with harvested content gaps, generate search terms for web harvesting.

Process:
1. Review placeholder entries with status='placeholder' that need external content
2. For each topic area, generate 2-5 search terms that would find authoritative content
3. Cross-reference with domain_rankings from population_strategy to identify high-authority domains
4. Output search-terms.json mapping topics to search term arrays

Example: For a 'sound-design' layer topic 'warm', generate: ['audio warm sound definition', 'warm frequency range audio', 'warm filter settings synthesis']

Output: search-terms.json with {layer_name: {topic: [search_terms]}}

items.title: [Researcher] — Execute web harvest
items.conditional: Only if structured KB and web harvesting enabled
items.description:
Execute web harvesting using kb-harvest skill or equivalent backend.

Process:
1. Read search-terms.json to get target topics and search terms
2. Select backend: ddg+webfetch (default), websearch+webfetch, webfetch (direct URL), firecrawl (requires API key), or imported
3. For each topic, execute search and fetch content from top results
4. Extract structured content using entry schema
5. Apply quality_threshold from population_strategy (default 0.7)
6. Add harvested entries with source.backend, source.url, and source.confidence
7. Update manifest with harvested counts

If no backend is available (no web access in environment), this task completes with a note that manual content addition is required.

Output: kb/ web-harvested entries, updated manifests, harvest-log.json

items.title: [Builder] — Create bridge entries
items.conditional: Only if bridge layer was defined in Phase 2
items.description:
Create bridge entries per bridge-schema.json for the most common translation mappings identified in research. Each bridge entry maps a subjective descriptor to technical parameters.

Minimum: one bridge entry per identified descriptor category from research/domain-analysis.md.

Verify: bridge entries conform to bridge-schema.json, all required fields present, confidence scores assigned (0.0-1.0).

EXECUTION: If bridge entries span multiple descriptor categories, work one category at a time. Complete all entries for the first category, then proceed to the next. Do not attempt all categories in a single response.

items.title: [Auditor] — Validate file paths and schema conformance
items.description:
Before the gate check, validate:

1. File-path audit: every file referenced in master-index.json and per-layer manifests exists on disk. Report any orphaned references or missing files.
2. Schema conformance: load entry-schema.json, then validate every KB entry against it. Check ALL required fields, types, and values — including entry ID format. If entry-schema.json defines an ID pattern (e.g., {kb}_{topic}_{entry-name}), every entry ID must match it. Do not accept ad-hoc ID formats that diverge from the schema.
3. If bridge layer exists: load bridge-schema.json and validate every bridge entry. Check confidence scores are numeric and in range [0.0, 1.0].
4. KB registry validation: if structured KB, verify kb-registry.json exists and contains metadata for all layers. Check that each layer entry has name, path, domain_boundary, authority_score, and topics.
5. Web harvest validation: if web harvesting was enabled, verify harvest-log.json exists and lists source URLs, backends used, and confidence scores for each harvested entry.
6. Artifact-manifest audit: verify artifact-manifest.md lists every file produced in this phase. Count files on disk and compare to manifest entry count. Report any untracked files.

Produce a validation-report.md listing: files checked, schema violations found (with entry ID and field), manifest gaps, registry issues, and a PASS/FAIL summary. This report is evidence for the gate.

items.title: [Architect] — Define phase structure for the output playbook
items.description:
Phase design principles:
1. Each phase is a coherent block of work with a clear objective
2. A phase's output is the next phase's input
3. Every phase ends with a gate — explicit approval criteria before proceeding
4. Early phases: understanding (audit, research). Middle: doing (build, create). Late: verifying and operating (QA, launch, monitor)
5. Cross-cutting concerns woven into relevant phases, not isolated

items.title: [Architect] — Define task granularity standard
items.description:
A task represents ONE deliverable or ONE decision. If a task takes more than 4 hours or requires multiple skill sets, split it. If a task can't fail independently of the next task, merge them. Every task must be completable by the assigned role without ambiguity.

Title-only vs description rules:
- TITLE ONLY: simple, obvious actions
- SHORT DESCRIPTION: tasks with specific requirements
- DETAILED DESCRIPTION: tasks requiring methodology, syntax, decision criteria, or multi-step procedures

items.title: [Architect] — Map phase dependencies
items.description: For each phase: hard dependencies (must complete first), soft dependencies (should complete), parallel opportunities (can run simultaneously). Within phases: which tasks block others.

items.title: [Architect] — Design phase gates
items.description:
For each phase: what must be TRUE before the next phase starts, what deliverables must exist, what quality checks must pass.

Gate conditions must be VERIFIABLE, not subjective:
- Good: 'All 15 city pages have 300+ words of unique localized content'
- Bad: 'City pages are done'

Each gate includes blocker_examples — specific scenarios that would prevent advancement.

items.title: [Architect] — Identify early assessment/detection phases needed
items.description: Does this domain have variable starting conditions that affect the workflow? Does detection change the workflow? Does the playbook need an environment setup phase? Does it need a deconstruction/audit phase before implementation? If yes, design these as dedicated phases BEFORE any implementation work.

items.title: [Architect] — Define the deliverable document tree
items.description: Which tasks produce documents, file path/naming conventions, which documents feed into later tasks. Every task that says 'Document in X' must have X defined here.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Review and approve architecture
items.description: Phase structure covers the full process. No gaps between phases. Phase gates are meaningful, not rubber stamps. Task granularity matches target user capability. Architecture satisfies all requirements from research/requirements.md.

Architecture satisfies requirements.md

Gates are vague ('research done') — make verifiable

Role names use consistent bracket syntax [RoleName]
Handoff points documented for all role transitions
Escalation paths defined for blocker types

items.title: [Architect] — Derive candidate roles from the work (task-driven)
items.description:
Do NOT start from a fixed role list. Cluster the Phase 4 process (and the tasks it implies) along four axes, then let roles fall out of the clusters:
1. Domain expertise required (what must this actor KNOW)
2. Decision authority (what may this actor DECIDE / approve / gate)
3. Tools & access (what may this actor TOUCH — repos, deploy, secrets, external services)
4. Independence (must this actor be separable from another — e.g. a checker must not check its own work)

Treat the six-role library {Stakeholder, Researcher, Architect, Builder, Auditor, Coordinator} as a PALETTE, not a mandate: base a role on one, ADD a new domain-custom role, REPLACE a generic role with a specialist, or DROP one that no task needs. Name every role in [RoleName] bracket syntax (custom names are expected, e.g. [DSPEngineer], [SecurityAuditor], [Deployer], [GameDataSync]).

Output: a candidate role list where each role is justified by the exact task-cluster it exists to own. A role with no cluster does not get created; a cluster with no owner is a missing role.

items.title: [Architect] — Engineer each role as an optimal agent spec
items.description:
For every derived role, write the canonical agent spec that Phase 7 will COMPILE into per-provider agent files. Per role:
- description: one-line responsibility
- role_context: the mindset / operating posture (how this agent thinks and what it refuses)
- decision_authority: what it may decide alone vs. must escalate
- tools: capabilities/access it needs (and, by omission, is denied)
- owns / owned_phases: the tasks or phases it is accountable for
- interfaces: {consumes: [...], produces: [...]} — the artifacts in and out
- agent_assignment: single | parallel | swarm
- defaults: {model: <tier frontier|high|fast>, temperature: [lo, hi]}

The spec is CANONICAL and provider-neutral (model is a capability tier, not a model id). It is the single source of truth; the compiled agent file (Phase 7) is a build artifact re-derivable from it. Match model tier to the role's hardest task, not its average one.

items.title: [Architect] — Apply the balanced minimality gate + mandatory invariants
items.description:
BALANCED MINIMALITY: prefer the smallest team that cleanly owns the work. Complexity-based guidance caps (not hard limits): simple ~3 roles, standard ~5, complex ~7. You MAY exceed a cap when a task-cluster genuinely needs distinct expertise, authority, or access that no existing role should hold — but justify each specialist in one line. Merge any two roles whose clusters differ only cosmetically. Delete any role that owns fewer than ~2 tasks unless independence requires it to exist.

MANDATORY INVARIANTS (every produced team, regardless of size):
1. Exactly one Coordinator-type role owns gates, tracking files, and blocker escalation.
2. At least one independent Verifier-type role (Auditor/Reviewer/QA/Verifier) that NEVER verifies an artifact it produced — the producer and the checker of any artifact must be different roles.
3. A human/Operator role wherever an irreversible action, a creative/product decision, or an external/public action lives (per the human-in-the-loop rule). Autonomy is not the goal.

Output: the final role roster with a one-line justification per role and an explicit note of which role satisfies each invariant.

items.title: [Architect] — Define handoff points and escalation paths over the derived roles
items.description: For each role transition: what artifact is transferred, in what format, and what constitutes a complete handoff (map to each role's interfaces.produces -> the next role's interfaces.consumes; every produced artifact must be consumed by someone or it is dead). Escalation: for each blocker class (technical, business/strategy, quality dispute, resource, scope) name the resolving role; terminal escalation is the human/Operator. No handoff may reference an undefined role.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: team derived, engineered, and invariant-complete
items.description: Verify the team is derived from the work (not copied), specced for compilation, and satisfies the invariants. Orphan/duplicate task-ownership is re-checked in Phase 9 after tasks exist.
gate_conditions: Every role is justified by a concrete task-cluster (no role without work; no cluster without an owner)
Every role has a compilable agent spec (description, role_context, decision_authority, tools, interfaces, agent_assignment, defaults)
Balanced minimality applied: role count within complexity guidance, or each over-cap specialist justified in one line
INVARIANT: exactly one Coordinator-type role owns gates/tracking/escalation
INVARIANT: an independent Verifier exists and no artifact is verified by its producer
INVARIANT: a human/Operator role owns every irreversible/creative/external decision
Handoff points documented for every role transition; every produced artifact is consumed
Escalation paths defined for every blocker class, terminating at the human

A produced artifact no role consumes, or a consumed artifact no role produces — fix the handoff graph

compilation.role_mindset: Builder — writing concrete tasks, not designing structure. Every task must be executable by reading title + description alone.
compilation.objective: Write all task titles, descriptions, gates with handoff blocks, and weave cross-cutting concerns throughout
success_criteria: All tasks written with titles and descriptions per granularity standard
Implementation methods specified on all technical tasks
Every phase has a compilation block and gate task with handoff block
Cross-cutting concerns appear in 3+ phases each
No placeholder text anywhere

items.title: [Builder] — Apply the validator's task-authoring rules
items.description: Every task owner MUST be [Role] bracket format (e.g. [Builder]) and match the role named in the task title. Every phase's compilation.context_load MUST include decisions-ledger.md and artifact-manifest.md. These are enforced by validate_playbook.py; authoring to them here avoids Phase 10 rework (audit F4).

items.title: [Builder] — Write all task titles
items.description:
Title format: [Role] — Action verb + specific deliverable

Rules:
1. Start with [Role] bracket
2. Use action verbs: Build, Create, Configure, Audit, Validate, Document, Review, Deploy, Test, Fix
3. Be specific: "Build homepage" not "Work on homepage"
4. Include quantity or scope where relevant
5. Every title must be understandable without reading the description

EXECUTION: Work one output-playbook phase at a time. Start with Phase 0, write all task titles for that phase, then proceed to Phase 1, and so on. Append each phase's titles to drafts/task-list-v0.1.md as you go. Do not attempt to write all phases in a single response — complete one phase per response, then continue to the next. This prevents output truncation on large playbooks.

items.title: [Builder] — Write task descriptions for all non-obvious tasks
items.description:
WHEN to include: task has specific requirements, requires methodology, has acceptance criteria beyond "done", involves a non-obvious process, or could be misinterpreted.
WHEN to skip: task is self-explanatory from its title alone.

Description format: Start with what the task produces. Then list any specific requirements, methodology, or acceptance criteria. Keep descriptions concise — 2-5 sentences.

EXECUTION: Work one output-playbook phase at a time. Write descriptions for Phase 0 tasks, then Phase 1, and so on. Update drafts/task-list-v0.1.md incrementally. Do not attempt all phases in a single response.

items.title: [Builder] — Include implementation method on all technical tasks
items.description:
For every implementation task, specify: which tools/interfaces to use, where content/data lives, what scope the edit has.

EXECUTION: Work one output-playbook phase at a time. Add implementation methods to Phase 0 tasks, then Phase 1, and so on. Update drafts/task-list-v0.1.md incrementally. Do not attempt all phases in a single response.

items.title: [Builder] — Include risk levels on tasks that affect shared resources
items.description:
Any task that edits a global or shared element must include: SCOPE (isolated / template-level / global), BLAST RADIUS (what else could break), ROLLBACK (how to undo if it fails).

EXECUTION: Work one output-playbook phase at a time. Review Phase 0 tasks for shared-resource risk, add risk annotations, then proceed to Phase 1, and so on. Skip phases with no shared-resource tasks. Update drafts/task-list-v0.1.md incrementally. Do not attempt all phases in a single response.

items.title: [Builder] — Write phase compilation blocks and gate tasks with handoff blocks
items.description:
Every phase opens with a compilation block: context_load, role_mindset, objective, pre_check, failure_modes_relevant.

Every phase closes with a gate task: gate_conditions (measurable, binary), blocker_examples (what failure looks like), handoff block (output_artifacts, next_phase_context, excluded_files, context_update).

EXECUTION: Work one output-playbook phase at a time. Write the compilation block and gate for Phase 0, then Phase 1, and so on. Update drafts/task-list-v0.1.md incrementally. Do not attempt all phases in a single response.
items.output: drafts/task-list-v0.1.md (updated with compilation blocks and gates)

items.title: [Builder] — Map and embed cross-cutting concerns into tasks
items.description:
Two-step process:

STEP 1 — CCC MAPPING: Create a mapping document listing each cross-cutting concern and the specific phases + tasks where it applies. For each CCC, identify at least 3 phases (minimum_phases requirement). Format:
  CCC-01: Quality Standard → Phase 6 task X, Phase 9 task Y, Phase 10 task Z
  CCC-02: Role Consistency → Phase 5 task X, Phase 6 task Y, ...

Write the full mapping to drafts/ccc-mapping.md before proceeding to Step 2.

STEP 2 — EMBEDDING: Work one CCC at a time. For each CCC, go through its mapped tasks and add a concrete verification checklist item to the task description. The checklist item must be a specific yes/no check, not a restatement of the concern.

Example: CCC "Quality Standard" applied to a task-writing task becomes:
  "Verify: every task has [Role] owner, every non-obvious task has description, no placeholder content remains"

After embedding all items for one CCC, move to the next CCC. Do not attempt all CCCs in a single response.

A CCC that appears in fewer than 3 phases after mapping is an audit failure — find additional phases where it applies before proceeding.

items.title: [Builder] — Create per-phase execution guides for critical phases
items.description:
For each phase marked critical in the process architecture, produce a standalone execution guide (phases/phase-N-name.md) containing: overview, purpose, pre-checks, task-by-task instructions with KB lookups where applicable, gate criteria, and common pitfalls.

Execution guides are more usable than raw JSON for human developers. Not every phase needs one — only phases with complex multi-step procedures or domain-specific judgment calls.

EXECUTION: Write one execution guide per response. Start with the first critical phase, write its complete guide, then proceed to the next. Do not attempt all guides in a single response.

items.title: [Builder] — Create reusable templates for key deliverables
items.description:
For each phase that produces a structured document (specification, test plan, review checklist, audit report), create a blank template with the expected structure, headings, and placeholder prompts.

Templates lower the barrier for developers executing the playbook by showing exactly what a completed deliverable looks like.

EXECUTION: Create one template per response. Start with the most critical deliverable template, then proceed to the next. Do not attempt all templates in a single response.

items.title: [Auditor] — Review all tasks for completeness and clarity
items.description:
Binary verification checklist:
- Does each task have a [Role] owner? Y/N
- Is each title specific and actionable? Y/N
- Do non-obvious tasks have descriptions? Y/N
- Do technical tasks have implementation methods? Y/N
- Do shared-resource tasks have risk levels? Y/N
- Are cross-cutting concerns woven into at least 3 phases each? Y/N
- Does every phase have a compilation block and gate? Y/N

EXECUTION: Audit one output-playbook phase at a time. Run the full checklist against Phase 0, document findings, then Phase 1, and so on. Compile all findings into a single review summary. Do not attempt to audit all phases in a single response.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: All tasks engineered
items.description: Produce a GATE VERIFICATION block: list each condition below with explicit PASS or FAIL and a one-line evidence citation (file path or content reference). A single FAIL blocks advancement to Phase 7.
gate_conditions: All tasks written with titles and descriptions per granularity standard
Implementation methods specified on all technical tasks
Risk levels assigned on shared-resource tasks
Every phase has a compilation block with context_load, role_mindset, objective, pre_check, failure_modes_relevant
Every phase has a gate task with handoff block
Cross-cutting concerns appear in 3+ phases each
Execution guides produced for all critical phases (phases/*.md)
Templates produced for phases with structured deliverables (templates/*.md)
[Auditor] review passed with no unresolved issues
No placeholder text anywhere
blocker_examples: A task says 'Build the dashboard' with no description — violates granularity standard, needs WHAT/HOW/SPECS/VERIFY
Cross-cutting concern only appears in the design phase — must also appear in build, QA, and monitoring phases
Gate handoff lists next_phase_context but no excluded_context — handoff is incomplete
No execution guides produced for complex phases — execution guides lower execution failure rate

output_artifacts: drafts/task-list-v0.1.md (includes all gate definitions with handoffs)
excluded_files: Task engineering discussion and iterations — final tasks captured in task-list
Auditor review notes — issues resolved, fixes applied

guardrail_checks: Task count matches complexity_profile.process dimension from Phase 0 — simple: 30-60 tasks, standard: 60-150, complex: 120-300 — if outside range, confirm with [Stakeholder] before proceeding

checklists.title: Phase 7: Output Configuration
checklists.purpose: Define how the output playbook is used: workflow model, session strategy, KB mapping, skill activation, router, and post-run review guidance.

compilation.role_mindset: Architect — designing how the playbook operates, not what it contains
compilation.objective: Define workflow model, usage instructions, session strategy, KB mapping, skill activation, router, and post-run review
pre_check: All tasks engineered with titles and descriptions
cross-cutting concerns woven into 3+ phases each
success_criteria: Workflow model defined with justification
Usage instructions cover start, session breaks, and context carry
Phase-to-KB-layer mapping consistent with KB layer definitions
Compilation block tuning (success_criteria, tools_available, behavioral_profile) specified for output playbook phases
Router/dispatcher defined
Post-run review structure defined

items.title: [Architect] — Define workflow model and role descriptions
items.description: Workflow model: human-in-the-loop, fully autonomous, human-directed, or custom. Role descriptions for the output playbook (from Phase 4 role definitions, condensed for the JSON).

items.title: [Architect] — Compile role specs into per-provider agent files
items.description:
Compile each canonical role spec (Phase 5, architecture/role-specs.md) into concrete agent definitions for the target provider(s). The spec is the source of truth; these files are build artifacts.

- Claude Code: emit .claude/agents/<role>.md with YAML frontmatter — name, description, model (resolved from the role's tier via defaults.providers[provider]), tools (from spec.tools) — and a system-prompt body built from role_context + decision_authority + interfaces.
- OpenAI Codex: emit an equivalent role-prompt file (model from the codex provider profile, gpt-5.5).
- Generic: emit an agents/manifest.json mapping role -> {tier, tools, system_prompt} for any other runner.

These compiled agents ARE the execution team that runs the OUTPUT playbook. Record the compilation target and the tier->model resolution in the output config so the team is reproducible. If the output workflow_model is single-agent, the compilation still emits the specs but notes one agent switches role_context per phase.

When commission_source=session_history, the roles derived from the harvest compile the same way — the produced update-playbook therefore ships with its own execution team, not just a role list.

items.title: [Architect] — Define usage instructions
items.description: How to start: what context to provide for the first phase. Session strategy: which phases can share a session, where to break, what context to carry. Cost optimization: how to minimize token usage while maintaining quality. General operating rules that apply to all phases.

items.title: [Architect] — Define compilation block tuning for output playbook phases
items.description:
For each phase in the output playbook, specify optional compilation block fields that tune agent behavior:

- success_criteria (array of strings): What the agent must produce/achieve — surfaced at phase START as a checklist
- tools_available (array of strings): Capability restriction — prevents role bleed by limiting what the agent can do
- behavioral_profile (object): Phase-specific tuning with four dimensions: risk_tolerance (minimal|low|moderate|high), creativity_level (strict|conservative|moderate|exploratory), verbosity (minimal|concise|detailed|comprehensive), stance (supportive|neutral|critical|adversarial)

These fields are optional — only add them where the default behavior would be wrong. Research phases benefit from higher creativity; validation phases need strict/adversarial stance.

EXECUTION: Work one output-playbook phase at a time. Define the compilation tuning for Phase 0, then Phase 1, and so on. Write each phase's tuning to output-config.md incrementally. Skip phases where defaults are sufficient — just note "defaults" for that phase. Do not attempt all phases in a single response.

items.title: [Architect] — Define phase-to-KB-layer mapping
items.description:
For each phase in the output playbook: which KB layers are relevant. No phase loads the entire KB — only the layers it needs. Must be consistent with KB layer definitions from Phase 2.

If structured KB with kb-registry.json: reference layers by name from the registry. The registry provides authority scores for ranking query results. Document any cross-layer queries that need weighted result merging.

Output: output-config.md with phase_kb_mapping referencing registry layer names.

items.title: [Architect] — Define skill activation mapping
items.description: For each phase: which prompting skill/mode to activate (or 'none'). Must be consistent with the skill field in each gate's handoff block. For new domains without existing skills, all values are 'none'. Skills are identified after execution runs and added in subsequent playbook versions.

items.title: [Architect] — Define router/dispatcher and context preservation specification
items.description:
Router: a short prompt or decision tree at the entry point. Given a user request, the router determines: which KB layers to load, which playbook phase applies, and which skill to activate.

For single-layer/flat KB playbooks: router is trivial.
For multi-layer KB playbooks: router maps request type to minimum KB slice.

Context preservation: define the two persistent files for the output playbook (decisions ledger and artifact manifest) — file paths, format, update rules, what never to exclude. File paths must match what compilation blocks reference in context_load.

items.title: [Architect] — Define post-run review structure
items.description: What to assess after the output playbook completes a run: what went well, what didn't, what should change, metrics target vs actual, quality assessment. This is guidance, not a template.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Output configuration complete
gate_conditions: Workflow model defined
Roles defined with responsibilities and decision authority
Usage instructions cover how to start, where to break sessions, what context to carry
Phase-to-KB-layer mapping is consistent with KB layer definitions from Phase 2
Skill activation is defined for every phase (even if 'none')
Router/dispatcher defined (or explicitly trivial for flat-KB playbooks)
Compilation block tuning defined for each phase (success_criteria, tools_available, behavioral_profile — omitted only where generic behavior is acceptable)
Post-run review structure defined
blocker_examples: Phase-to-KB-layer mapping references a layer not defined in Phase 2 — reconcile
Skill activation inconsistent with gate handoff skill fields — fix one or the other
Usage instructions don't explain how to start the first session — add initial context guidance

excluded_files: Session strategy rationale — captured in output-config.md
Alternative workflow models considered — final choice documented

checklists.title: Phase 8: Metrics & KPI Definition
checklists.purpose: Define measurable success criteria for the output playbook.

compilation.role_mindset: Researcher — defining what success looks like, not building it. Domain outcome metrics require understanding what the playbook is supposed to achieve.
compilation.objective: Define process, output quality, and domain outcome metrics with targets and measurement methods
pre_check: KB mapping and skill activation defined
success_criteria: At least one process metric defined with measurement method
At least one output quality metric defined with measurement method
At least one domain outcome metric defined with measurement method
All metrics have title, description, type, and target
Stakeholder approved metrics and targets

items.title: [Researcher] — Define process metrics
items.description:
Metrics measuring the execution of the playbook itself: duration metrics (time to complete, time per phase), volume metrics (tasks completed, deliverables produced), quality metrics (issues found at QA, rework count, gate failures).

For each: title, description, type (metric_integer | metric_currency | metric_duration), category ('process'), target, measurement method.

items.title: [Researcher] — Define output quality metrics
items.description:
Metrics measuring the QUALITY of the work produced: gate pass rate, audit findings count, description completeness, domain-specific quality measures.

For each: title, description, type, category ('output_quality'), target, measurement method.

items.title: [Researcher] — Define domain outcome metrics
items.description:
Metrics measuring whether the playbook achieved its PURPOSE. These are entirely domain-specific (downloads, revenue, coverage, compliance score, etc.). For optimization playbooks: include BEFORE and AFTER variants.

At least one metric in this category is mandatory — a playbook without outcome metrics can't prove it worked.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Review and approve metrics
items.description: Metrics align with business goals from Phase 0. Targets are ambitious but achievable. Every metric has a clear measurement method. At least one metric in each of the three categories.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Metrics defined and approved
gate_conditions: At least one process metric defined
At least one output quality metric defined
At least one domain outcome metric defined
All metrics have title, description, type, and measurement method
Targets set where applicable
[Stakeholder] approved
blocker_examples: No domain outcome metric defined — a playbook that can't prove it worked is incomplete
Metric has no measurement method — define how to measure before proceeding

excluded_files: Metric alternatives discussed and rejected — final metrics captured
Task granularity and dependency docs — content reflected in the task list

guardrail_checks: Metrics count matches complexity_profile from Phase 0 — simple: 3-5 metrics, standard: 5-10, complex: 8-20 — if outside range, confirm with [Stakeholder] before proceeding

checklists.title: Phase 9: JSON Assembly
checklists.purpose: Assemble the complete output playbook JSON from all design documents. This phase focuses on assembly and syntax — structural validation happens in Phase 10.

compilation.role_mindset: Builder — assembling JSON from source documents. Mechanical precision, no creative interpretation.
compilation.objective: Assemble the complete output playbook JSON with all 16 required top-level fields and validate syntax
pre_check: At least one metric per category defined
success_criteria: JSON parses without errors
All 16 required top-level fields present
All checklists have title, purpose, compilation, and non-empty items array
Every item has title and owner fields

size_guidance.timeout_risk: Write tool has ~60 second timeout for large content
size_guidance.chunking_strategy: Write structure first (title through roles), then use Edit to append sections. Never write >500 lines in single Write call.

items.title: [Builder] — Estimate JSON size
items.description:
Calculate estimated line count before writing to determine if chunked writing is required.

ESTIMATION FORMULA:
- Base structure: ~200 lines (title, version, description, workflow_model, defaults, roles, scope)
- Each phase (checklist): ~50 lines (title, purpose, compilation, items, gate)
- Cross-cutting concerns: ~15 lines each
- Failure modes: ~10 lines each
- Metrics: ~10 lines each
- Usage instructions: ~50 lines

Total = 200 + (phases × 50) + (CCCs × 15) + (FMs × 10) + (metrics × 10) + 100

If estimated total > 500 lines, use chunked writing strategy.

Output: One line in size-estimate.md: 'estimated_lines: N'

items.title: [Builder] — Start from the schema + template
items.description: Read templates/output-schema.json and copy templates/output-template.json as the starting skeleton. The template already carries the exact, easy-to-miss shapes (audit F2): handoff={output_artifacts:[],next_phase_context:[]}; cross_cutting_concerns[].id matches ^CCC-\d{2}$ with enforcement_method in {checklist_items,gate_condition,compilation_precheck,task_description}; failure_modes[].id matches ^FM-\d{3}$ and phase is a STRING; phase_kb_mapping and skill_activation need ONE entry per phase; usage_instructions requires how_to_run, session_strategy, cost_optimization, and post_run_review.assess[]; every task owner is [Role] bracket format; every phase context_load includes decisions-ledger.md and artifact-manifest.md. Fill the template rather than authoring shapes from memory.

items.title: [Builder] — Write JSON header and structure
items.description:
Write the top-level JSON structure using the Write tool. Include: title, version, description, phase_summary, workflow_model, defaults, knowledge_base, roles.

CRITICAL: Write tool has ~60 second timeout. For outputs >500 lines estimated, this task writes ONLY the header/structure. Use Edit tool for subsequent sections.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
```json
{
  "title": "...",
  "version": N,
  "description": "...",
  "phase_summary": [...],
  "workflow_model": "...",
  "defaults": {...},
  "knowledge_base": {...},
  "roles": {...}
}
```

Do NOT close the JSON yet. Leave it open for subsequent sections.

items.title: [Builder] — Append cross_cutting_concerns and failure_modes
items.description:
Use Edit tool to append cross_cutting_concerns array and failure_modes array after the roles section.

Each CCC must have: id, title, description, enforcement_method, enforcement_rule, minimum_phases, phases_applied.
Each FM must have: id, symptom, root_cause, fix, prevention, phase, severity, source.

EXECUTION: Single Edit call to append both sections. Keep each section under 200 lines.

items.title: [Builder] — Append checklists (phases array)
items.description:
Use Edit tool to append the checklists array containing all phases.

Each phase must have: title, purpose, compilation block (context_load, role_mindset, objective, pre_check, failure_modes_relevant), items array with tasks, and gate task.

CHUNKING: If checklists array is >300 lines, append in 2-3 Edit calls:
1. Append checklists opening and first half of phases
2. Append remaining phases
3. Close the checklists array

items.title: [Builder] — Append metrics, usage_instructions, and remaining sections
items.description:
Use Edit tool to append: metrics array, usage_instructions object, phase_kb_mapping object, skill_activation object, router object, context_preservation object, then close the JSON.

Each metric must have: id, title, description, type, category, target, measurement_method.

Close the JSON with proper bracket nesting.

items.title: [Builder] — Validate JSON syntax
items.description:
Parse without errors. No trailing commas, unescaped characters, mismatched brackets. All string values properly escaped.

Verification: python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('playbook.json'))"

If validation fails, return to writing tasks to fix syntax.

items.title: [Auditor] — Validate assembled JSON structure and cross-references
items.description:
Before the gate check, validate the assembled playbook JSON:

1. Structural completeness: verify all 16 required top-level fields exist. For each checklist, verify title, purpose, compilation (with context_load), and non-empty items.
2. Cross-reference integrity: every file in a compilation.context_load must appear in a prior phase's handoff.output_artifacts or be a tracking file. Every [Role] in a task title must exist in roles{}.
3. ID format checks: FM-NNN, MET-NN, CCC-NN patterns. No duplicates.
4. Gate completeness: every phase has exactly one gate with gate_conditions, blocker_examples, and handoff block.

Run validate_playbook.py and validate_semantic.py if available. Fix all errors before proceeding.

EXECUTION: If the playbook is large, validate in sections: first top-level fields and roles, then checklists one phase at a time, then metrics/failure_modes/mappings. Do not attempt to review the entire JSON in a single response.

items.title: [Builder] — Self-validate against output-schema.json (jsonschema) before handoff
items.description: Before Phase 10, run a local jsonschema check against templates/output-schema.json and fix every error. This catches shape errors without depending on the external validator. Command: python3 -c "import json,jsonschema;s=json.load(open('templates/output-schema.json'));d=json.load(open('<draft>.json'));[print(list(e.path),e.message) for e in jsonschema.Draft7Validator(s).iter_errors(d)]"  — zero output = pass.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: JSON assembled and syntactically valid
items.description: Produce a GATE VERIFICATION block: list each condition below with explicit PASS or FAIL and a one-line evidence citation (file path or content reference). Reference structural-validation.md for cross-reference evidence. A single FAIL blocks advancement to Phase 10.
gate_conditions: JSON parses without errors
All 16 required top-level fields present
All checklists have title, purpose, compilation, and non-empty items array
Every item has title and owner fields
Structural validation: all cross-references resolve and no orphaned references
Artifact-manifest.md lists drafts/playbook-v0.1.json and structural-validation.md

automated_checks: python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('drafts/playbook-v0.1.json')); assert len(d.get('checklists',[])) > 0, 'No checklists'; print(f'{len(d["checklists"])} phases')"
gate_verification.verification_script: Parse JSON, count top-level fields (expect 16), count checklists, verify each has title+purpose+items. Report counts.

items.stakeholder_question: The assembled playbook has N phases and M total tasks. Does this match your expectations for this domain's complexity?
