Missing required top-level field — check the 16-field checklist
Automated JSON parse check fails — fix syntax errors before proceeding

excluded_files: All source documents — consolidated into JSON
KB specification docs — embedded in JSON knowledge_base section

checklists.title: Phase 10: JSON Validation & Consistency
checklists.purpose: Validate the assembled JSON using automated validators and manual review. Fix all structural, role consistency, and schema errors before proceeding to quality audit.

compilation.role_mindset: Auditor — validating with fresh eyes. The JSON was assembled in a previous session; now verify it independently.
compilation.objective: Run automated validators, fix all errors, then manually review for logical flow and clarity issues validators cannot catch
success_criteria: validate_playbook.py passes with zero errors
validate_semantic.py passes with zero errors
Manual review passed

items.title: [Auditor] — Run automated validation and fix all errors
items.description:
Run validate_playbook.py and validate_semantic.py against the assembled JSON. If jsonschema is available, also run with --schema templates/output-schema.json. Fix all errors reported. Re-run until both validators pass with zero errors. Document any remaining warnings with explanations.

Covers: structural completeness, [Role] consistency, KB schema, compilation blocks, summary view consistency, failure_modes, metrics, CCC validation, handoff chain, and semantic checks.

items.title: [Auditor] — Manual review of assembled JSON
items.description:
Read through the playbook as a user would: Do tasks flow logically within each phase? Are descriptions consistent in tone and detail level? Would you know how to complete every task from title + description alone? Are metrics measurable with the tools/access defined?

EXECUTION: Review one phase at a time. Start with Phase 0, note any issues, then Phase 1, and so on. After reviewing all phases, review the non-checklist sections (metrics, failure_modes, roles, usage_instructions). Compile all findings into a single review document. Do not attempt to review the entire playbook in a single response.

items.title: [Auditor] — Verify CCC minimum phases
items.description:
For each cross-cutting concern, verify that phases_applied array has length >= minimum_phases.

AUTOMATED CHECK:
```python
import json
d = json.load(open('playbook.json'))
for ccc in d['cross_cutting_concerns']:
    if len(ccc['phases_applied']) < ccc['minimum_phases']:
        print(f"FAIL: {ccc['id']} has {len(ccc['phases_applied'])} phases, minimum is {ccc['minimum_phases']}")
```

Report any violations and ensure they are fixed before proceeding.

items.title: [Auditor] — Verify handoff chain integrity
items.description:
Verify that files referenced in context_load appear in earlier phases' handoff blocks.

FOR EACH PHASE N:
1. Check compilation.context_load lists files
2. Verify those files appear in handoff.output_artifacts of Phase N-1, N-2, etc.
3. Check that gate handoff.next_phase_context lists files
4. Verify those files are produced in the phase

BUILD PROVENANCE GRAPH:
- Track which phase creates each file
- Track which phase uses each file
- Report any files used but never created
- Report any files created but never used

AUTOMATED CHECK: If validate_playbook.py has --handoff-chain option, run it. Otherwise, trace manually.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: JSON valid and structurally complete
gate_conditions: validate_playbook.py passes with zero errors
validate_semantic.py passes with zero errors
Manual review passed — tasks flow logically, descriptions are clear, no ambiguity
CCC validation: all cross-cutting concerns have phases_applied.length >= minimum_phases (ccc-validation.md documents verification)
Handoff chain validated: all context_load files have creators in earlier phases (handoff-chain-validation.md documents verification)
blocker_examples: A [Role] appears in 2 task titles but is not in the roles{} section — undefined role, fix
phase_kb_mapping says Phase 3 uses 'dsp-kb' but no gate handoff references that layer — reconcile
CCC-02 has phases_applied with only 2 entries but minimum_phases is 3 — weave into additional phase
context_load references 'requirements.md' but no earlier phase produces it — add to handoff or remove from context_load
guardrail_checks: Total phases, tasks, roles, CCCs, and metrics are within complexity_profile guardrail ranges — if outside, confirm with [Stakeholder]

excluded_files: All intermediate drafts — consolidated into JSON
Validation logs — issues fixed

checklists.title: Phase 11: Quality Audit — Gap Analysis
checklists.purpose: Systematic audit of the assembled playbook against requirements, cross-cutting concerns, phase flow, contradictions, completability, detail calibration, and KB integrity. Produces a prioritized fix list.

compilation.role_mindset: Auditor — reviewing with fresh eyes, not defending previous work. Binary yes/no judgments, no hedging.
compilation.objective: Audit the playbook across all quality dimensions and compile a prioritized fix list
success_criteria: Comprehensive audit completed covering all 7 dimensions with documented findings
Fix list compiled and prioritized (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
All phases, roles, and cross-cutting concerns covered by the audit

items.title: [Auditor] — Comprehensive quality audit
items.description:
Audit the playbook across all quality dimensions in a single pass. For each dimension, document findings as PASS/FAIL with specifics:

1. Requirements coverage: For each requirement in research/requirements.md, is it addressed by at least one task? Any requirements only partially addressed?
2. Cross-cutting concerns: For each concern, how many phases reference it? Any concerns appearing in fewer phases than minimum_phases?
3. Phase-to-phase flow: Does Phase N's output fully satisfy Phase N+1's inputs? Any gaps in the handoff chain?
4. Contradictions: Any tasks contradicting strategic constraints, other tasks, or the implementation method?
5. Task completability: Is every task assignable and completable given its role, inputs, and description?
6. Detail calibration: Any simple tasks over-described? Any complex tasks under-described?
7. KB buildability: Can an agent build the KB from the spec alone? Any contamination risk between layers?

EXECUTION: Audit 2-3 dimensions per response. Start with dimensions 1-2, then 3-4, then 5-7. Append findings to audits/comprehensive-audit.md incrementally. Do not attempt all 7 dimensions in a single response.

items.title: [Auditor] — Compile audit findings into prioritized fix list
items.description: CRITICAL: contradictions, missing phases, broken dependencies. HIGH: cross-cutting gaps, incomplete descriptions, orphaned roles, unbuildable KB spec. MEDIUM: detail level issues, consistency problems. LOW: formatting, naming conventions, minor wording.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: All audits complete, fix list compiled
gate_conditions: Comprehensive audit completed covering all 7 dimensions
Fix list compiled and prioritized (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
All phases, roles, and cross-cutting concerns covered
blocker_examples: Requirements not covered — add tasks or clarify
Cross-cutting concern only in one phase — weave throughout
Phase gaps identified — add missing tasks

excluded_files: Audit detail — findings consolidated into fix-list.md

checklists.title: Phase 12: Stress Testing & Structured Dry-Run
checklists.purpose: Walk through the playbook under structured scenarios to find issues that gap analysis misses. Define a scenario matrix, execute walkthroughs from multiple perspectives, verify conditional logic and handoff chains, document friction, fix all issues, and get Auditor sign-off.

compilation.role_mindset: Auditor — adversarial thinking. Try to break the playbook by simulating real usage scenarios.
compilation.objective: Define scenario matrix, walk through the playbook under all scenarios, verify conditional logic and handoff chains, fix all issues
success_criteria: Scenario matrix defined with 2+ scenarios
All scenario walkthroughs completed
Handoff chain traced and verified
All CRITICAL, HIGH, and MEDIUM issues fixed
JSON re-validated after fixes
Auditor verification passed — no regressions

items.title: [Coordinator] — Define scenario matrix
items.description:
Define 2-3 scenarios with concrete parameters:

1. MINIMAL CASE: smallest possible project in this domain. Exercises the fewest tasks and conditional paths.
2. TYPICAL CASE: representative mid-complexity project. Exercises the most common path.
3. COMPLEX CASE (optional): high-complexity variant. Exercises conditional tasks, all KB layers, maximum role coverage.

For each scenario: name, brief description, which conditional tasks apply, expected KB complexity, expected number of phases exercised.

items.title: [Auditor] — Scenario walkthroughs
items.description:
For each scenario in the matrix, walk through every phase of the playbook:

Per-scenario checks:
- Can each task be completed given this scenario's parameters? Y/N
- What would the task produce for this scenario?
- Are there blockers, ambiguities, or missing information?
- Does the gate make sense for this scenario?

Scenario-specific perspectives to apply:
- Happy path: no problems — does it flow end to end?
- Domain novice: someone who has NEVER done this work — can they follow the tasks?
- KB construction: agent encountering domain for first time — can they build the KB from the spec?
- Blockers: what if access/tools are unavailable? What if QA fails?
- Domain variants: if the playbook covers variants, do all tasks make sense for each variant?

Document Y/N per task per scenario.

EXECUTION: Complete one scenario at a time. Walk through the entire playbook for Scenario 1 (minimal case), document findings, then Scenario 2 (typical case), and so on. Within each scenario, if the playbook has many phases, break at natural boundaries (e.g., phases 0-4, then 5-8, then 9+). Do not attempt all scenarios in a single response.

items.title: [Auditor] — Verify conditional logic and trace handoff chain
items.description:
Conditional task logic: For each conditional task, does the condition evaluate correctly for each scenario? Are there ambiguous conditions? Missing conditional tasks?

Handoff chain trace: For each scenario, trace the full chain from Phase 0 to final phase. Does each phase's next_phase_context provide everything the next phase needs? Are there context_load items that no previous phase produces? Does the context budget allow loading all critical files at every phase?

EXECUTION: Complete conditional logic verification first (one scenario at a time), then handoff chain tracing (one scenario at a time). Do not attempt all scenarios in a single response.

items.title: [Auditor] — Edge cases and friction documentation
items.description:
Edge cases: minimal case (smallest project) — does it still work? Maximal case (largest, most complex) — does it scale? Legacy case (old technology/process) — does it accommodate? Partial case (project starts mid-stream).

Friction log: all questions that arose, ambiguities found, tasks needing more detail, tasks in wrong order, missing tasks.

Failure mode catalog: for every issue discovered, create FM entry (symptom, root_cause, fix, prevention, phase, severity, source).

items.title: [Builder] — Fix all issues from audit and stress testing
items.description: Resolve all issues in audits/fix-list.md, starting with CRITICAL, then HIGH, then MEDIUM. After each fix, verify no new contradictions introduced. For each fix: note what changed, verify the fix doesn't break anything else. Add new failure modes to failure_modes[] for issues discovered during testing.

items.title: [Builder] — Re-validate and produce tested JSON
items.description: Run validate_playbook.py and validate_semantic.py. Verify JSON parses, all roles consistent, compilation blocks intact, handoff chains unbroken. Save validated output as drafts/playbook-v0.2.json.

items.title: [Auditor] — Verify all fixes and sign off
items.description:
Verify: all fixes are clean — no new contradictions, no regressions. JSON still validates. KB specification still buildable. Handoff chain still intact for all scenarios. Fix-list entries are resolved, not just closed.

If issues found: return to [Builder] for fixes, then re-verify. Do not advance.

items.title: [Auditor] — Optional pilot execution (execution-grounded validation)
items.description: For BUILD/EXECUTION-type domains, a paper walkthrough is not enough (audit F3). Where feasible, execute the produced playbook's first phases (or one representative task per phase) against a scratch/throwaway target and record MEASURED evidence that it runs and produces the intended artifact. 'Runs and works' outranks 'reads consistently'. Skip only for purely advisory/document domains, and record why in decisions-ledger.md.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Stress testing and dry-run complete
items.description: Produce a GATE VERIFICATION block: list each condition below with explicit PASS or FAIL and a one-line evidence citation (file path or content reference). A single FAIL blocks advancement to Phase 13.
gate_conditions: Scenario matrix defined with 2+ scenarios
All scenario walkthroughs completed with Y/N per task per scenario
Conditional task logic verified for all scenarios
Handoff chain traced and verified for all scenarios
Edge cases and friction documented
All CRITICAL, HIGH, and MEDIUM issues fixed
JSON re-validated after fixes
[Auditor] verification passed — no regressions
Dry-run fidelity: at least one phase has a mock output demonstrating the playbook is executable

automated_checks: grep -c 'Y\|N' testing/scenario-walkthroughs.md  # verify per-task Y/N entries exist
gate_verification.verification_script: Verify all 7 output artifacts exist with >0 bytes. Parse playbook-v0.2.json. Count Y/N entries in walkthroughs.

items.stakeholder_question: Review the friction log — which items would block a first-time user? Should any be promoted to must-fix before release?
blocker_examples: Scenario walkthrough reveals unresolvable ambiguity in a task
Handoff chain broken — phase N+1 needs file that phase N doesn't produce
CRITICAL issue found that requires architectural change (escalate to Stakeholder)
Automated file-existence checks fail for testing/ deliverables — complete the walkthroughs before advancing

excluded_files: Scenario walkthrough details — issues extracted and fixed
Pre-fix JSON draft — superseded by v0.2

checklists.purpose: Final human review before pilot testing.

compilation.role_mindset: Stakeholder — business alignment, strategic review. Does this playbook achieve what was commissioned?

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Review playbook against business strategy
items.description: Does the playbook produce the right outcome? Are strategic constraints respected throughout? Are metrics aligned with business KPIs? Is the playbook parameterized properly (per-run variables, not hardcoded)? Would you trust this playbook to run without supervising every step?

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Review roles and ownership
items.description: Roles match available capabilities. No role is overloaded. Decision authority is correctly placed. Coordination role has enough visibility.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Provide feedback and change requests
items.description:
Specific, actionable feedback: tasks to add, remove, or modify; description changes needed; phase structure changes; metric or target adjustments.

'Make it better' is not feedback. Specific changes only.

items.title: [Builder] — Implement stakeholder feedback

items.title: [Builder] — Re-validate JSON after changes

items.title: [Auditor] — Verify stakeholder changes don't introduce regressions
items.description: Spot-check that feedback implementation is clean — no new contradictions, no broken handoffs. Verify compilation blocks still consistent after any phase structure changes. If issues found: return to [Builder], then re-verify.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Final approval of playbook
items.description: Satisfies success criteria from Phase 0. All feedback addressed. Business strategy respected throughout. Would you run this playbook tomorrow with confidence?

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Stakeholder approved, Auditor verified

[Auditor] verification passed — no regressions from changes
Roles and ownership reviewed — no overloaded roles, decision authority clear
Final approval given
JSON valid after changes
Success criteria from Phase 0 are satisfied
blocker_examples: Stakeholder says 'looks fine' without reviewing specific phases — not approval, need documented review
Feedback says 'add more detail to Phase 3' without specifying which tasks — not actionable, request specifics

Previous draft versions — superseded

checklists.title: Phase 14: Documentation & Version Control
checklists.purpose: Package the final playbook with supporting documentation.

compilation.role_mindset: Coordinator — packaging and archiving. Completeness and clarity for future users.
compilation.objective: Create changelog, archive research/audit docs, store production JSON, write quick-start guide

Production JSON stored in designated location with backup

items.title: [Coordinator] — Create playbook changelog
items.description: Version history with dates and change summaries: v0.1 (initial draft), v0.2 (post-audit fixes), v0.3 (post-stakeholder feedback), v1.0 (post-pilot, production ready).

items.title: [Coordinator] — Compile final metrics report
items.description:
Read metrics-tracker.md. For each metric: compare final value against target from the metrics[] array. Produce a summary table:

| Metric | Target | Actual | Status |

Status: PASS (met target), MISS (below target), N/A (no target defined).

Include brief analysis: which metrics indicate process health, which indicate output quality, what to improve in the next run.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Documentation complete

Research and audit docs archived
JSON in version control
Quick-start guide covers prerequisites, how to start, key roles, and phase overview
Final metrics report compiled with target vs actual comparisons
All files listed in artifact-manifest.md exist at their specified paths

gate_verification.verification_script: Verify all 4 final/ files exist with >0 bytes. Parse playbook-v1.0.json. Verify research/, audits/, testing/ directories exist and are non-empty.

items.stakeholder_question: Does the quick-start guide make sense to someone who wasn't involved in building this playbook? Would you hand this to a colleague and expect them to succeed?

Automated file-existence checks fail for final/ deliverables — create missing files before closing

checklists.title: Phase 15: Continuous Improvement
checklists.purpose: After each completed run of the output playbook, review and optionally improve it. Manual and human-initiated — no automatic feedback loops.

compilation.role_mindset: Stakeholder — reviewing execution data, deciding what to change
compilation.objective: After each playbook run, collect review data, catalog failure modes, decide whether to update the playbook
pre_check: At least one run of the output playbook has been completed
success_criteria: Run review data collected and documented
New failure modes cataloged with proper FM-IDs
Stakeholder decision on updates recorded in decisions-ledger.md
If updates approved: changes implemented and JSON re-validated

items.title: [Coordinator] — After each playbook run: collect review data
items.description: Review the post-run assessment (using the post_run_review structure from Output Configuration). Compare actual metrics to targets. Note tasks consistently skipped, reordered, or added ad-hoc. Note where the KB spec was insufficient during construction.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Catalog failure modes from this run
items.description:
For every bug, crash, unexpected behavior, or degraded result encountered during the run: create a failure mode entry (id: FM-NNN sequential, symptom, root_cause, fix, prevention, phase, severity, source).

severity: crash (process cannot continue), error (wrong output), degraded (works but quality reduced), cosmetic (visual/formatting).
prevention: write as a concrete checklist item or gate condition.
phase: assign to the output playbook phase where this should be prevented or detected.

Add entries to failure_modes[] array. Update relevant phase compilation blocks with new FM-IDs.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Decide whether to update the playbook
items.description: Review collected data and new failure modes. Decide: update now, update later, or no changes needed. If updating: specify what changes to make and why. This is a human decision — the agent does not auto-modify the playbook.

items.title: [Builder] — Implement playbook updates
items.description: Follow same quality standards: validate JSON, check structural completeness, verify no introduced contradictions. Integrate failure mode prevention items into relevant phase tasks or gate conditions. Update changelog.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Improvement cycle complete
items.description: Validate that the improvement cycle has been executed: run data collected, failure modes cataloged, and any approved updates implemented and re-validated.

New failure modes cataloged with FM-IDs (or 'none found' documented)
Stakeholder decision on updates is recorded in decisions-ledger.md
If updates approved: changes implemented and JSON re-validated

New failure modes described in prose but not formatted with FM-ID, severity, and prevention fields

how_to_run: Load this playbook as context for a planning session
CRITICAL: Before starting Phase 0, read the phase_summary field to understand all 16 phases. Do NOT begin execution until you can name every phase.
A single agent fills all roles — switch mental context per phase
Work through phases sequentially — each phase gate must pass before the next
For each task: read the title and description, complete the work, verify completion
At phase gates: verify all conditions are met, collect metrics_snapshot if present, then proceed

Context management: this playbook file may exceed your context window. Use the phase_summary field as a navigation index. When entering a new phase, re-read that phase's checklist from the JSON rather than relying on memory of earlier reads.
Final output: a domain-specific playbook JSON following output-schema.json
session_strategy: Phases 0-1: Share a session (scoping and research are tightly coupled)
Phases 2-3 (KB Architecture + Bootstrapping): Share a session — design then build
Phase 4 (Process Architecture): Fresh session with new eyes on structure
Phases 5-6 (Role + Task Engineering): Share a session — roles inform task writing
Phases 7-8 (Output Config + Metrics): Share a session
Phase 9 (JSON Assembly): Dedicated session — heaviest context load
Phase 10 (JSON Validation): Fresh session — validate with fresh eyes
Phases 11-12 (Gap Analysis + Stress Testing): Share a session — audit pair
Phase 13 (Stakeholder Review & Iteration): Human review gate — break session here for genuine stakeholder input
Phase 14 (Documentation & Version Control): Package final playbook with supporting docs
Phase 15 (Continuous Improvement): Post-run review and optional playbook updates
context_management: Phases 0-1 share context (scoping + research are tightly coupled)
Phases 2-3 share context (architecture design then bootstrapping)
Phase 9 is context-heavy (JSON assembly loads all design documents) — consider fresh session
If context warning appears, summarize decisions-ledger.md and start fresh session
Always persist decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, metrics-tracker.md before session break
Phase 10 benefits from fresh eyes — validate with new session, not immediately after Phase 9
cost_optimization: Use compilation blocks — only load what the phase needs
Respect excluded_context — don't re-load what was deliberately dropped
For large playbooks: break JSON Assembly into multiple sessions (assemble, then validate)
Audit phases benefit from fresh context — don't carry forward build-phase thinking

assess: What went well in the process
What should change in the playbook
Metrics: target vs actual for every defined metric
Quality assessment: were gates effective, were tasks clear, were roles right
Catalog any failure modes encountered during the run

execution_modes: SINGLE-AGENT (default): one agent fills all roles, switching mental context per phase. Best for context-heavy runs where the scoping/research context must persist across phases (the JSON is one coherent build). This is the model usage_instructions.how_to_run assumes.

ROLE-AGENT (optional): dispatch the dedicated pbcpb-* agents (pbcpb-stakeholder/researcher/architect/builder/auditor/coordinator) per phase for independent, less-anchored review. Use when you want adversarial separation (e.g. an independent Auditor at Phases 11-12) and can afford re-briefing context across agents. Do not mix mid-phase; pick one mode per run and record it.

failure_modes.symptom: KB architecture designed in Phase 2 but no directory, placeholders, or entries exist after creation completes
failure_modes.root_cause: No phase executes the KB blueprint — Phase 2 designs it, but building was out of scope
failure_modes.fix: Execute Phase 3 (KB Bootstrapping) to create directory tree, seed placeholders, harvest initial entries
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 3 gate verifies KB directory exists with populated entries before advancing

failure_modes.symptom: Cross-cutting concern appears in only 1-2 phases despite 3+ minimum requirement
failure_modes.root_cause: Weaving instruction is vague — 'must appear in 3+ phases' without specifying enforcement method
failure_modes.fix: Check each CCC's phases_applied array, add enforcement to additional phases until minimum_phases met
failure_modes.prevention: CCC objects have enforcement_method and phases_applied fields; Phase 10 validates count >= minimum_phases

failure_modes.symptom: Task title uses [Human] but owner field says 'human' — role validation fails
failure_modes.root_cause: Inconsistent bracket syntax between title and owner field during manual JSON assembly
failure_modes.fix: Normalize all owner fields to bracket syntax matching title: owner must be '[Role]' not 'Role' or 'role'
failure_modes.prevention: Validation script checks owner field matches [Role] in title exactly

failure_modes.symptom: KB layers defined as JSON array instead of named keys — agents cannot look up layers by name
failure_modes.root_cause: Entry schema says 'layers' but doesn't specify whether it's an array or object
failure_modes.fix: Restructure layers as named keys in the knowledge_base object, or as array of objects with required 'name' field
failure_modes.prevention: KB schema validation task explicitly checks layer structure format

failure_modes.symptom: Failure mode entries missing required fields (title or description) — FM references are broken
failure_modes.root_cause: FM entry schema not enforced during manual assembly
failure_modes.fix: Add all required fields to each FM entry: id, symptom, root_cause, fix, prevention, phase, severity, source
failure_modes.prevention: Validation script checks all 8 required FM fields, FM-ID pattern, and no duplicates

failure_modes.symptom: Metrics missing ID fields — cannot cross-reference from tasks or gates
failure_modes.root_cause: Metric schema did not require an ID field
failure_modes.fix: Assign sequential MET-NNN IDs to all metrics
failure_modes.prevention: Validation script checks metric ID uniqueness and MET-NNN format for v3+ playbooks

failure_modes.symptom: Cross-cutting concerns stored as plain strings — no enforcement metadata, no tracking of where they're applied
failure_modes.root_cause: CCC schema only required a description string, not structured enforcement data
failure_modes.fix: Convert each CCC string to object with id, title, description, enforcement_method, enforcement_rule, minimum_phases, phases_applied
failure_modes.prevention: Validation script checks CCC object structure, phases_applied count >= minimum_phases

failure_modes.symptom: Phase N+1 context_load references file not in Phase N's next_phase_context — handoff chain gap
failure_modes.root_cause: Handoff blocks assembled manually without systematic chain verification
failure_modes.fix: Trace full handoff chain and add missing files to next_phase_context or remove from context_load
failure_modes.prevention: Validation script checks handoff chain consistency (check 16); dry-run protocol traces chains for all scenarios

failure_modes.symptom: Gate handoff skill_validation field references wrong phase's skill — 10 mismatches found
failure_modes.root_cause: Gates were copied between phases and skill field not updated
failure_modes.fix: Audit every gate's skill_validation against the phase it hands off TO, not the current phase
failure_modes.prevention: Stress testing scenario traces skill activation chain; validation script checks skill_activation consistency

failure_modes.symptom: KB layer directories missing from context_load — 12 directories not loadable
failure_modes.root_cause: KB directories referenced in phase_kb_mapping but not in compilation block context_load
failure_modes.fix: Add all referenced KB directories to relevant phase context_load arrays
failure_modes.prevention: Validation script cross-checks phase_kb_mapping against context_load; stress test verifies KB access per phase

failure_modes.symptom: All 13+ context_load files at priority 5 — budget system cannot make intelligent loading decisions
failure_modes.root_cause: Priorities assigned uniformly without considering which files are core vs reference-only
failure_modes.fix: Differentiate priorities: 5 for core inputs, 4 for section-specific, 3 for reference, 1-2 for persistent tracking files
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 9 and 10 split into assembly (heavy context) and validation (light context); priorities differentiated per file importance

failure_modes.symptom: Pilot testing is a mental walkthrough, not real execution — misses runtime issues
failure_modes.root_cause: Real pilot requires multiple sessions outside the creation context, which is impractical
failure_modes.fix: Use structured dry-run protocol with scenario matrix, phase-by-phase walkthrough, handoff chain trace
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 14 gate accepts either structured dry-run (2+ scenarios) OR real pilot; dry-run protocol is systematic and documented

failure_modes.symptom: Task description says 'build X' without method, specs, or verification — task is unexecutable
failure_modes.root_cause: Task granularity standard not enforced during task writing
failure_modes.fix: Add WHAT/HOW/SPECS/VERIFY structure to all non-obvious task descriptions
failure_modes.prevention: Auditor review in Phase 6 uses binary checklist: does each description answer what, how, and how to verify?

failure_modes.symptom: 4-layer bridged KB designed for a domain that could use a flat folder — massive over-engineering
failure_modes.root_cause: No complexity assessment before KB design; defaults to maximum complexity
failure_modes.fix: Re-evaluate using Phase 2 Task 1 complexity questions; switch to flat if warranted
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 0 complexity classifier sets knowledge dimension; Phase 2 gate guardrail_checks flag mismatches

failure_modes.symptom: Playbook scope covers all variants (effects + instruments + synthesizers) instead of common case with conditionals
failure_modes.root_cause: Scope definition didn't distinguish primary path from variant paths
failure_modes.fix: Define primary scope (common case), mark variant-specific tasks as conditional
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 0 scope task explicitly requires primary/variant distinction; complexity classifier informs scope breadth

failure_modes.symptom: Metrics defined with targets but never measured during execution — metrics are decorative
failure_modes.root_cause: No measurement task in gates, no tracking file, no collection mechanism
failure_modes.fix: Add metrics_snapshot to gate handoff blocks; initialize metrics-tracker.md in Phase 0
failure_modes.prevention: metrics_snapshot.collect lists metric IDs to record at each gate; metrics-tracker.md persists across sessions

failure_modes.symptom: failure_modes array empty after first execution — no guidance when things go wrong
failure_modes.root_cause: Cold start problem: v1.0 playbooks have no execution history to draw failure modes from
failure_modes.fix: Seed failure_modes with entries from first execution; update failure_modes_relevant in affected phases
failure_modes.prevention: v4 creator ships with 26 seeded FMs from first execution; Phase 15 catalogs new FMs from each run

failure_modes.symptom: Phase N requires Phase M's output but Phase M requires Phase N's — circular dependency
failure_modes.root_cause: Dependency map not validated for cycles during process architecture
failure_modes.fix: Break the cycle by reordering phases or splitting the shared dependency into a prerequisite phase
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 4 dependency mapping task requires DAG proof (no circular dependencies); validated in architecture review

failure_modes.symptom: project-state.json referenced in tasks and gate handoffs but never created by any task
failure_modes.root_cause: File referenced before a creation task was written for it
failure_modes.fix: Add initialization task or remove all references
failure_modes.prevention: Artifact provenance validation (check 17) catches files in context_load not produced by any prior phase

failure_modes.symptom: Context compaction at session boundary loses critical details — decisions and rationale silently dropped
failure_modes.root_cause: Session strategy doesn't account for LLM context window compaction behavior
failure_modes.fix: Ensure all critical decisions are persisted in decisions-ledger.md before session breaks
failure_modes.prevention: Session strategy aligns breaks to phase gates where decisions-ledger is updated; context_preservation rules enforce persistence

failure_modes.symptom: success_criteria contradicts gate_conditions — agent works toward targets that the gate doesn't verify, or gate checks things not in success criteria
failure_modes.root_cause: success_criteria and gate_conditions authored independently without cross-checking
failure_modes.fix: Review each success_criteria entry against gate_conditions — every criterion should map to at least one gate condition
failure_modes.prevention: Cross-validation check 19 warns when success_criteria count and gate_conditions count diverge significantly (ratio < 0.3 or > 3.0)

failure_modes.symptom: tools_available too restrictive — agent cannot perform required tasks because a needed capability is not listed
failure_modes.root_cause: tools_available authored without checking what capabilities each task actually requires
failure_modes.fix: Walk through each task description and verify the tools_available list covers all required capabilities
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 10 validation audits tools_available against task descriptions — flag tasks that imply capabilities not in the list

failure_modes.symptom: tools_available too permissive — lists capabilities not needed by the phase, defeating role bleed prevention
failure_modes.root_cause: tools_available copied from another phase without trimming to actual needs
failure_modes.fix: Remove capabilities not required by any task in the phase
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 12 stress testing verifies each tools_available entry is actually used by at least one task in the phase

failure_modes.symptom: behavioral_profile mismatch — phase has adversarial stance but tasks require constructive building, or supportive stance on an audit phase
failure_modes.root_cause: behavioral_profile authored based on role name rather than actual phase activities
failure_modes.fix: Review behavioral_profile against phase purpose and task types — stance must match the work being done
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 10 validation cross-checks behavioral_profile.stance against role_mindset role name (Auditor phases should not be supportive, Builder phases should not be adversarial)

failure_modes.symptom: Orphaned success_criteria — criteria exist but phase has no gate_conditions to verify them, so success is declared without checking
failure_modes.root_cause: success_criteria added to compilation block but gate task not updated to match
failure_modes.fix: Add corresponding gate_conditions for each success_criteria entry, or remove criteria that are not verifiable
failure_modes.prevention: Cross-validation check 19 catches phases where success_criteria exists but gate_conditions is empty or missing

failure_modes.symptom: Executing agent completes early phases (0-3) in detail but produces only summaries or skips later phases entirely. Final output is a skeleton, not an executable playbook.
failure_modes.root_cause: Playbook file exceeds the agent's practical context window. Agent reads only the first few phases and synthesizes the rest from imagination. No mechanism forces the agent to acknowledge or re-read later phases before execution.
failure_modes.fix: Use the phase_summary field as a navigation index. Re-read each phase's checklist from the JSON before executing it. The Phase 0 inventory task ensures all phases are acknowledged before work begins.
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 0 gate requires phase inventory acknowledgment (all 16 phases listed in decisions-ledger.md). Context management guidance in usage_instructions directs re-reading per phase.

failure_modes.symptom: Context overflow occurs mid-run without warning. Post-overflow quality degrades — agent stops referencing specific research content and produces generic claims.
failure_modes.root_cause: No context budget estimation during Phase 0. Session breaks not planned around overflow risk. The design-to-assembly transition (Phase 8→9) is the highest-risk overflow point.
failure_modes.fix: Estimate context budget in Phase 0. If estimated total exceeds model window, plan mandatory fresh session at Phase 8/9 boundary with explicit state serialization.
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 0 context budget estimation task (added in v5). Session breaks aligned to phase gates. decisions-ledger.md updated before every session break.

failure_modes.symptom: Agent self-assesses gate conditions as PASS when deliverables don't exist. 4+ phases false-passed in trial-2.
failure_modes.root_cause: No automated verification — agent is both producer and verifier. Self-assessment bias: the agent that did the work assumes it succeeded.
failure_modes.fix: Add gate_verification blocks with automated file-existence and JSON-parse checks. Require minimum_automated_ratio of 0.5. Applies to EVERY phase gate (cross-cutting).
failure_modes.prevention: CCC-08 (Automated Gate Verification) enforces automated checks at 50%+ of gate conditions. gate_verification blocks added to critical phases.

failure_modes.symptom: KB placeholder seeding completed but harvesting skipped entirely. Agent treated mechanical seeding as full bootstrapping.
failure_modes.root_cause: Seeding (mechanical/Builder) and harvesting (analytical/Researcher) grouped under single phase with single gate. Agent optimized for gate passage by completing the easier task.
failure_modes.fix: Add seeding milestone gate within Phase 3. Change harvesting task owner from [Builder] to [Researcher]. Add explicit gate conditions checking zero remaining placeholders for harvestable content.
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 3 now has milestone gate between seeding and harvesting. Harvesting task uses [Researcher] role. Phase 3 final gate checks placeholder count = 0 for harvestable entries.

failure_modes.symptom: Web harvest task fails or produces no results despite valid search terms
failure_modes.root_cause: Selected backend is unavailable in execution environment (e.g., firecrawl requires API key, web access blocked)
failure_modes.fix: Fall back to next available backend. If no backends work, mark search terms as pending and proceed with research-only harvest. Document in harvest-log.json that web harvest was attempted but failed.
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 2 should specify backend fallback order. Phase 3 harvest task should check backend availability before attempting web harvest.

failure_modes.symptom: KB registry references layers that don't exist, or KB layers exist but aren't in registry
failure_modes.root_cause: kb-registry.json created during bootstrapping but not updated when layers were added/removed, or manual edits to KB without registry update
failure_modes.fix: Re-run Phase 3 Register KB layers task to sync registry with actual directory structure. Validate registry against master-index.json.
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 3 gate checks kb-registry.json exists and contains all layers. Any KB modification must update registry.

failure_modes.symptom: Produced playbook copies the six library roles verbatim regardless of domain; roles don't match the actual work
failure_modes.root_cause: Phase 5 treated the role library as a mandate instead of a palette; roles not derived from task-clusters
failure_modes.fix: Re-run Phase 5 derivation: cluster tasks by expertise/authority/tools/independence and let roles fall out of the clusters; rename to domain-custom roles.
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 5 gate requires each role justified by a concrete task-cluster; a role with no cluster is not created.

failure_modes.symptom: A role both produces an artifact and signs off its verification; nothing independently checks that work
failure_modes.root_cause: No independent Verifier invariant enforced; producer self-verifies
failure_modes.fix: Split the role into a producer and an independent Verifier (Auditor/Reviewer); route the artifact's gate to the Verifier.
failure_modes.prevention: CCC-11 + Phase 5 gate: assert producer != verifier per artifact class and that an independent Verifier exists.

failure_modes.symptom: Task owner references a role that isn't defined, a role is defined but owns no task, or a task has no owner
failure_modes.root_cause: Roles derived separately from tasks and never reconciled; team does not exactly cover the work
failure_modes.fix: Reconcile owners against the role roster: define the missing role, drop/merge the idle role, or assign the ownerless task.
failure_modes.prevention: CCC-10 + validate_semantic team-completeness check run at Phase 9/10.

failure_modes.symptom: A role produces an artifact no one consumes, or consumes one no one produces; handoff graph has dangling edges
failure_modes.root_cause: Handoffs authored per-role without checking the produce/consume graph closes
failure_modes.fix: Map every interfaces.produces to a downstream interfaces.consumes; add the missing producer/consumer or delete the dead artifact.
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 5 gate: every produced artifact is consumed; no handoff references an undefined role.

failure_modes.symptom: A compiled agent file (.claude/agents/*.md or codex prompt) has drifted from its canonical role spec — different model tier, tools, or authority
failure_modes.root_cause: Agent file hand-edited after compilation instead of re-compiled from the spec
failure_modes.fix: Re-compile the agent from architecture/role-specs.md; treat the spec as canonical and the agent file as a build artifact.
failure_modes.prevention: Phase 7 records the tier->model resolution; agent files are regenerated, never hand-edited.

failure_modes.symptom: Produced playbook carries top-level sections the schema doesn't define (e.g. domain_patterns, domain_catalog) as if they were the contract, or role/metric shapes drift from output-schema.json
failure_modes.root_cause: Author worked from a remembered/prose copy of the contract instead of loading templates/output-schema.json
failure_modes.fix: Author against the loaded schema and fill templates/output-template.json; move genuinely extra data into a KB layer (kb_mode=USER_SUPPLIED), not into invented top-level fields.
failure_modes.prevention: CCC-01/contract fidelity: Phase 9 loads output-schema.json + output-template.json and self-validates before Phase 10 (audit F2).

failure_modes.symptom: Session harvest is taken as fact — uncited or single-occurrence patterns become hard rules that then gate the build
failure_modes.root_cause: Harvest ingested without verifying citations or occurrence counts
failure_modes.fix: Phase 1 ingest verifies each item's citation, flags single-occurrence patterns, and reuses PBCPB's FM/CCC catalogs before minting new ids.
failure_modes.prevention: CCC-12 (evidence traceability): uncited items dropped/flagged; single-occurrence marked 'verify in future runs'.

failure_modes.symptom: The front-end prompt's output is returned without ever running the validators; schema/semantic errors ship (reintroducing the drift the audit fixed)
failure_modes.root_cause: Standalone one-shot generation with no validate-to-green loop
failure_modes.fix: Run validate_playbook.py --no-trace --schema and validate_semantic.py (or scripts/harvest_session.py check) and iterate until both pass before returning.
failure_modes.prevention: Updater mandates the validate loop; Phase 10 re-runs it as the gate.

router.description: The playbook creator is mostly sequential. Two conditional inputs at the front (commission_source) and one KB branch at Phase 1->2 (kb_mode). A raw session history is distilled by the front-end prompt into a harvest, then built and verified by the full pipeline — not emitted one-shot.
decision_tree: New playbook commission → Start at Phase 0

Commission from a raw AI-dev session history -> run prompts/playbook-updater.md to produce research/session-harvest.md, set commission_source=session_history at Phase 0; Phase 1 ingests + validates it, then Phases 4-15 derive roles, assemble, validate, audit, and dry-run as normal.
Resume interrupted run → Check artifact-manifest.md for latest phase, resume there
Post-run improvement → Go directly to Phase 15

After Phase 1: check scope.md kb_mode → if PLAYBOOK_MANAGED: proceed to Phase 2 → Phase 3 → Phase 4. If EXTERNAL_DIFY_MCP, USER_SUPPLIED, or NONE: skip Phase 2 and Phase 3, proceed directly to Phase 4.
router.default: Start at Phase 0 with a commission brief

context_preservation.decisions_ledger: decisions-ledger.md — append-only, one paragraph per phase gate: phase number, key decisions, constraints discovered, rejected alternatives with brief rationale
context_preservation.artifact_manifest: artifact-manifest.md — running index of every file: path, producing phase, status (active|superseded|archived), one-line summary
context_preservation.metrics_tracker: metrics-tracker.md — running log of metric values collected at phase gates. Columns: Metric ID | Phase | Value | Target | Date
rules: All three files are initialized in Phase 0 and updated at relevant gates
decisions-ledger.md and artifact-manifest.md are always included in context_load — exempt from token optimization cuts
metrics-tracker.md is included in context_load only for phases whose gates collect metrics
At session breaks, verify all three files are saved and current before ending
If context compaction occurs mid-session, these files serve as ground truth for recovering state
Configuration decisions (output location, external data sources) from scope.md are ALWAYS loaded in context
If scope.md is missing configuration section, halt and request Phase 0 completion
